chapters.title: Chapter 151: The 21 Trinkets of a Goddess
paragraphs: "But just because the master now knows he may be a reincarnation from the past doesn’t mean the master can tell anyone. That is not allowed—at least, not yet," Akira said, making Kent nod.
He knew some things were meant to be hidden.
"Gaia, use 500,000 Tower points to build a place you two can spend time with Li Hua. By the way, do you two eat, or are you robots?" Kent asked.
Akira and Gaia smiled at his childish question.

"We are cosmic beings, master, not robots. And yes, I eat. I don’t know about Gaia, though. She uses universal energy as her food, so she might just be one of those weirdos," Akira said, jumping behind Kent when she felt Gaia’s glare on her.
"Tsk. I eat, master. In fact, I’ve been meaning to try some banana cakes, but since I wasn’t supposed to reveal myself until this bitch appeared, I didn’t get the chance," Gaia replied.
"Good, then. Use the points I gave you to build a house for the three of you. Of course, if it’s not enough, then do it since you’ll be living in it," Kent said with a grin.
The only thing on his mind now was how the fuck things had taken such a sudden turn.
But then again, he had already seen freaky when he awakened a Night Rider and an Aetherwarden. Having Weavers wasn’t something to freak out about.

"Also, the master cannot tell anyone about our existence. For now, I am just a Tower assistant, and that idiot is a Soul Sentinel. Only the master can know about our true existence since we told him."
Kent nodded at Gaia’s words. The last thing he wanted was danger following him because he chose to become a loudmouth.
"Off you go, then. I will come to the Harem Tower later." Gaia and Akira entered the tower, leaving Kent to recollect his thoughts.
A lot had just happened, but he wasn’t about to let it overwhelm him. For now, he knew Gaia was more than just a tower, so he could only use this advantage.
"It doesn’t matter. I must first check the trinkets Vexthra gave me." Kent retrieved the space ring she had given him.
"This one is much better than mine," Kent said, taking his own off. He then placed the one Vexthra had given him onto his finger. He looked inside, and, well, there were dozens of items.
"She really went all out for mere trinkets," Kent chuckled before pouring everything onto the bed. There were 21 items in total.
Four swords, a dagger, a bow, a staff, eight pieces of armour, and six necklaces. Kent quickly used [Enchanted Eyes] to appraise the items, but what he saw left his jaw hanging loose.
"That is a lot of soul items you have there, master. Do you want me to weave some upgrades into them? I’ll just take 21 soul crystals," Akira said, appearing suddenly in the room.
"Akira, shouldn’t you be planning your new home with Gaia? What are you doing here?" Kent asked though he wasn’t dismissing her presence or offer.
"This is just a strand of my consciousness. All weavers can do that. I can even help you with that if your soul becomes strong enough," Akira replied as she began turning the soul items on the bed.
"The one who created these things might really love you very much. It’s full of divine energy," Akira said, making Kent smile.
"She is indeed my first woman and the one who brought me to this world. Of course, I know you knew that already, considering you are a weaver," Kent just sighed.
Gaia and Akira seemed to shift his perspective on things now.
"You are not wrong. But I can’t know everything, master. Unless you give me permission, I cannot do as I please," Akira replied, still meticulously checking the items.
"However, I know enough to know this bow is for your wife, called Unity. Don’t ask me how I know. The name of the bow is [Unity’s Divine Bow], with a skill called [That’s My Sister]."
"Your first wife certainly has a sense of humour. She is also a good Artisan since she was able to create such a perfect, soul item." Akira seemed impressed.
Kent just smiled and checked the swords. Three didn’t have names, but one already had a name, and well, it’s her humour that counted here.
[My Man]
That was the name Vexthra gave the sword, and for a moment, Kent couldn’t stop his mouth from twitching. The goddess seems to have a lot of free time on her hands.
But they were all good items. The three other swords were yet to be named. Also, the dagger was for Kent, for obvious reasons.
But he didn’t reject it.

As for the armour, they were the same, but from what he saw in the appraisal, they were made to adapt to the user’s preferences. This meant it would become a cloak if he wanted it to appear like a cloak.
However, the buffs in the armours were just too good to reject. Kent even wondered why something like this would be allowed in the mortal realm.
But who was he to question something good?
As for the necklaces, they were life-saving items that could be charged using soul energy. They all have the same effects in them. There are three effective abilities in them.
The first one is called [Cosmic Shield]. It creates a cosmic shield around the user, protecting them from any sudden attacks. Of course, the user can activate it with a thought—at will.
It is also automatic in case the user isn’t aware of a sudden attack.

The second is [Cosmic Blast]. This one creates a cosmic blast from the energy stored in the necklace. The blast can kill opponents three realms above the owner, making it, in a way, a perfect killing weapon.
However, this depends on how much energy the necklace has stored before the blast.
Akira even mentioned that it would take some time to accumulate enough energy, but with the runes inscribed in the necklace, the blast would be several times more powerful.
Kent could only thank his lover the next time they met.
The last effect is [Teleportation]. The user must create an anchor somewhere safe, and they can teleport back to it in times of emergency.
This, of course, is useful but not necessarily essential in his eyes.
He could escape any battle with the tower, or so he thought. According to Akira, the moment he engaged in combat, the chances of Gaia taking him away were very slim.
Doing so would affect him in some way. So, the necklace was the safest way for him and his women. This, of course, nearly made him open a portal to the god realm to have a moment with his goddess.

All 21 items were just too overpowered for someone in this middle-grade world. But who was he to complain? He tucked everything away and promised Akira he would let her know when he got the Soul Stones.
Of course, without any further weaving, the items were already powerful.
A few minutes later, he called his three women over, and then he called his master, too. It was time to send them to the tower.
Of course, he trusted his master enough to take her, too. But if she tried something funny, he would just obtain his first resource for his first Undead General...lol.

chapters.title: Chapter 152: The Third Night Rider
paragraphs: The Dark Devil Church - Athea Kingdom Branch
Hyx, the leader of the Althea branch of the Dark Devil Church, sat only on his bone throne like a king without his subjects.
A pitiful sight.
He was quiet, deep in thought, probably because he hadn’t heard from the men he sent to take care of the Alderford family.
Well, they were dead.
But he didn’t know that yet—it had only been a few hours since their deaths anyway. Oh, he didn’t know because he was confident his men would succeed.
But he was wrong. He had lost nine Root Sages and three Root Great Sages. Meanwhile, the ones in charge of the life crystals were debating who would deliver the news to their leader.

Undoubtedly, they wouldn’t be walking out of there alive. They would die, and none of them wanted to be the one to bring that fate upon themselves. So, they pretended they hadn’t discovered the 12 life tablets.
However, 12 hours after his men had died, he went to check on their life crystals. That was when he discovered they were dead.
That day, Hyx became enraged. Without a second thought, he flew out and headed toward Caprath City without reservations.
He planned to kill every last person associated with the events that began with Lady Sandra’s death. He had already lost enough, and because of that, he couldn’t think straight.
But he didn’t get far. In fact, he didn’t even leave the borders of Vastport City when he was stopped in his tracks by a man on an eerie-looking horse.
The man in question was clad in a dark cloth and a hood, with burning green eyes.
"Who are you?" Hyx asked, unleashing his level 3 Root Transcendent cultivation base. The entire space he was in was filled with a powerful presence that could break even Peak Root Great Sages

"It seems you have lost your way, Rider. But don’t worry, master has risen and he calls. You can stop living a life of deceit and schemes." Uncle Drew, in his Night Rider form, said, showing no sign he was being affected by the aura.
Hyx, who sensed this, was immediately enraged and punched forward.
However, before he could get within a meter of Uncle Drew, a flaming arrow arrived and exploded in his face. This forced him back, but as a Root Transcendent, he wasn’t injured.
But it hurt like hell.
He looked to his right and saw another dark figure sitting on yet another eerie horse. However, this one had a different design from the one Uncle Drew was sitting on.
"Who are you people?" Hyx asked again, his eyes bloodshot.
"Like the captain said, it’s time for you to ride again," Aria, the Archer Uncle Drew saved back in the Demon Mountains, said, looking eerie at Hyx.
She isn’t fully a Night Rider, but that doesn’t mean she can’t command the flames of hell to a certain extent.
The flames of hell are among the most powerful and lethal fires in the universe. A mere touch can be very agonizing.
Hyx chuckled, then raised his hand. A spell circle appeared in the air, six layers showing that he was casting a Tier 6 spell.

A large shard of ice appeared inside the circle, instantly shooting toward Uncle Drew while Hyx dashed toward Aria. However, strange-looking chains burst from the ground before he could move, grabbing hold of his legs.
The chains bonded his legs, preventing him from flying away.
As for the ice shard, Uncle Drew unleashed a sword attack that instantly severed the shard into countless pieces.
Hyx became even more enraged, and thus, he tapped into his strength and unleashed his trump cards.
"Come out and kill them!" the enraged Hyx shouted, and a portal opened.
From the portal, four spirit beasts appeared:
A flaming lion with a large horn.
A white tiger with golden stripes on its fur.
A giant-looking humanoid troll wielding a large club. The club seemed to be made of metal, and from how it looked, it was very durable and lethal.
The last one was a shadowy horse or perhaps a unicorn. However, the moment the shadowy figure appeared, Uncle Drew raised his hand, and a portal opened.
From the portal, flames poured out, immediately consuming the four beasts, with the shadowy beast being the last.
The creatures vanished as quickly as they had come, making Hyx look at the dark-cloaked figure in fear now. He could tell he was powerless in front of him.
Of course, he was. No Night Rider can attack their captain, regardless of their power. In front of him, they are ants.
But he was only prolonging his inevitable end.
He tried to wiggle his way out of the chains but couldn’t. His strength was slowly leaving his body.
Strangely, the two dark figures didn’t attack him.
They just stood there, watching him.
Two hours later, Hyx had lost all strength in his body. The chains of hell have drained all his strength.
"You have disobeyed the summoning of the Riders of the Night, so for your punishment, you will spend 200 years in the flames of hell."
Just when Hyx had given up, Uncle Drew spoke. The next second, the chains bound him completely, and a portal of flames appeared.
He was tossed in, taking his screams with him.
This sight seemed to have affected Aria, who immediately asked why. They had indeed come to take him and succeeded—so why punish him?
"That is the rule of the Night Riders. Those who refuse their summon will spend time in the flames of hell as repentance.
This is for his own good since being reborn by the flames of hell will mould them into who they are meant to be, making them much stronger."
"Then I want to enter there since my awakening isn’t complete yet," Aria said, moving close to Uncle Drew.
"Okay." He didn’t ask why. He just bound her in chains, and she, along with her shadowmare, was tossed into the flames of hell.
It was like Uncle Drew had expected something like that. But since being reborn from the flame seemed to have a good effect on them, he didn’t bat an eye.
The irony.
After they were gone, Uncle Drew transformed into his human form. The way he looked before inheriting the true name of a Night Rider.
His shadowmare also transformed into a carriage, which he laid down inside, whistling as if he hadn’t just sent two people to hell.
Twenty hours later, he transformed back into his Night Rider form and opened two portals. From within the portals, two people emerged. One was calm and looked much more dangerous.
The other was screaming like a bastard. Of course, Hyx entered as a mortal, not as a half-Night Rider, so he experienced the short end of the stick.
That day, Hyx Von Martin, who had spent 200 years in hell, learned that there are some things more painful than being cuckolded.
"With the Authority of the Riders of the Night, I summon you to stand and ride again into the night. Do you heed the call?" Uncle Drew asked, looking expressionless under his hood.
That day, the third member of the Night Riders has heeded the call. Soon, they will ride all over this world and beyond to summon back their brethren to ride into the night with them.

chapters.title: Chapter 153: The Three Soul Sentinels
paragraphs: Kent stood with his arms behind him as he gazed at four otherworldly beauties and Li Hua, who wore shocked expressions on their faces.

He had brought them to the tower, specifically to a garden where a treehouse could be seen. He had waited for two hours after Gaia and Akira went to build their home in the tower before bringing the five ladies inside.
The two Weavers seemed to have built a treehouse in the small garden. The place was very charming, and from its appearance, it was clear they had used the rarest kind of materials.
Kent regretted giving them the 500k Tower Points. He had expected a large house, but the two lolis seemed far more childish yet devious.
"Everyone, welcome to my personal domain," Kent’s words snapped them back to their senses, his lips curving into a faint, confident smile.
"Kent, what is this place?" Saintess Selene asked, her brows furrowed in confusion.
"This is my personal domain, which I, and only I, have control over. Nobody else—not even gods—can access it," Kent said, snapping his fingers with a sly smirk.
Suddenly, the two lolis appeared, startling everyone.
Gaia returned to her Fairy Pirate form, her expression as mischievous as ever, while Akira stood in her young, adorable form, her backpack still secured on her back.
"This is Gaia and Akira. They are my assistants," Kent explained, his gaze shifting to Gaia with a subtle nod.
"Well, she is more like my assistant for this place. As for Akira, I have a major position planned for her. But for now, just see them as my assistants."
Kent kept his expression neutral, carefully avoiding revealing the truth: they were Weavers, two of the three ever to grace this universe.
Although he knew the ladies in front of him had no idea who the Weavers were, Kent preferred it that way. It was for their own good—knowing too much could bring them unnecessary harm.
It also made things easier for Kent; he wouldn’t have to worry about his ladies accidentally revealing anything they shouldn’t.
"Hi, everyone! I’m Akira," Akira said cheerfully, extending her small hand for a handshake. Her innocent smile was infectious, yet there was a spark of mischief in her eyes.
Saintess Selene hesitated briefly, her gaze shifting between Akira’s hand and her face, before accepting the handshake with a slight nod.
"Hmm, what a powerful sword body... Too bad you haven’t even awakened or reached the first form yet," Akira remarked, tilting her head and flashing a knowing grin.
Saintess Selene’s eyes widened in shock, her lips parting as if to speak but no words came out.

"She has a knack for reading the innate nature of people," Kent interjected with a guilty smile, scratching the back of his head. He sighed inwardly, already envisioning the trouble Akira was bound to cause.
He approached Unity first, then Lilian, and finally stopped in front of Elsa.
"Can I see them? Your soul sentinels," she asked, her tone calm but carrying an air of certainty, as though she already knew everything about her.

Elsa glanced at Kent, searching for his reaction. The subtle anticipation on his face made her smile weakly, a faint blush colouring her cheeks. Kent seemed just as curious as Akira was about her soul sentinels.
His first summon was a troublemaker, and now he couldn’t help but wonder what kind of beings she had under her command. Elsa currently had three soul sentinels.
Elsa waved her hand, and three beings appeared - all Peak Root Sage experts.
One is a dark, robbed figure wielding daggers. Well, she has daggers sheathed on her waist and legs and some pointy knuckle weapons on her arms.
She wore a mask covering her mouth and nose and an eyeliner covering her eyes in black paint. She has next to no presence. It was like she didn’t have any aura or life running through her.
Kent appraised her and found out she was the SSS-class summon. A peak saint with powerful abilities. Strangely, she can upgrade her class as she climbs the cultivation chart.
⟪Name: Nyxira (The Silent Shadow) ⟫
- Race: Umbral Elf
- Rank: Root Sage (97%)
- Class: Shadow Assassin (SSS - upgradable)

After cleaning every part, she sat in the chair with Kent’s head resting on her boobs.
"So, Alina, aside from managing the auction house, what do you want to achieve as a cultivator?
I know you cherish your current role, but you most certainly have something you truly desire," Kent asked.
However, as the question left his mouth, he noticed a shift in Alina.
He felt it—the kind of shift that comes from old wounds.
It seemed he might have touched on something he shouldn’t have.
"You don’t have to answer if you don’t want to," Kent quickly added, gently rubbing her shoulder to reassure her.
Alina nodded, staying silent for a long five minutes before finally speaking.𝑓𝓇𝘦ℯ𝘸𝘦𝑏𝓃𝑜𝘷ℯ𝑙.𝑐𝑜𝓂
"I always wanted to become an Array Master.
In fact, I dreamed of it and even began studying before I became a cultivator.
But...
I don’t think I can follow that path anymore," she sighed, her expression heavy with defeat.
"Why?" Kent asked after a moment of hesitation.
Alina stood up and sat in the chair opposite him, facing him directly.
Kent, sensing the seriousness of the moment, stayed seated and attentive.
"Until the first son of the Miller Noble family is dead, I won’t be able to.
I want to drive my sword through his heart for what he did to me." Tears began to stream down her face as she clenched her fists, her voice trembling with anger and pain.
Kent wasn’t a magician, but he could tell something terrible had happened to her.
Even without knowing the details, he could vaguely grasp the weight of her words.
He waited patiently, giving her time to calm herself.
Eventually, Alina steadied her breathing and, with visible effort, began to tell Kent everything.
So it turns out she was the daughter of a maid in this noble family in the Varyndor Kingdom.
They were one of the richest and most powerful noble families in the kingdom, and her mom had served as a maid there for many years.
It was there she gave birth to her and cared for her until she turned 15 and began cultivating.
Back then, her mother did everything she could to provide for her and make sure she lacked nothing.
For years, she did an impeccable job.
However, when Alina turned 18 and started showing signs of being a genius, the head of the Miller family noticed this.
It ensured she officially joined the family so she could become one of their strengths in the future.
It seemed like a good thing for both her and her mother.
However, things turned dark when the Miller family’s first son, Turyn, set his sights on her.
He tried everything in his power to get her into his bed, but she refused every time.
Turyn, of course, never backed down.
There was only so much he could hold back, and eventually, he snapped.
One day, while Alina was alone, he snuck in and forcefully had his way with her.
It was a painful moment in her life.
But it became worse when she later discovered that her mom had been murdered by Turyn’s goons, who were keeping watch while he committed his sin.
Seeking justice, she went to the head of the family to report him.
But they didn’t believe her, and in the end, she was cast out of the family after they ensured her spirit root was sealed.
This meant she couldn’t continue levelling up.
But that changed when she met Kent, and through dual cultivation, she started to level up again.
Also, the seal on her spirit root was broken, which suggested Kent’s yang qi held profound mysteries.
Despite that, her trauma prevented her from walking the path she had always wanted.
Though brilliant, she couldn’t use her Rune Knife to draw arrays after that incident.
Since then, she has resigned to manage the auction house alone.
As time passed, she gradually accepted and began living her new life enthusiastically.
"So it seems I need a new quest, then.
I will deliver this bastard to you on a silver platter.
All you have to do is prepare your sword," Kent said, taking her into his arms.

chapters.title: Chapter 158: Leaving Caprath City
paragraphs: "Don’t worry, I will make sure that bastard doesn’t live long enough to enjoy his days," Kent said with a smile, holding Alina in his arms. It took him two hours, but he managed to calm her down.
Her trauma was much deeper than he had thought. But for now, he planned to make sure she got her revenge. And since the universe also wanted that, who was he to reject it?
He quickly checked the quest.
⟪You have received a new question from the Universe Quest Pool.⟫
-> Quest Name: Overdue Revenge
-> Quest Type: Side Quest
-> Quest Difficulty: High
-> Quest Duration: 30 days
-- Use any means necessary to deliver the one named Turyn to the one Named Alina on a silver platter. It doesn’t matter how you go about it; you just get him.
<Rewards>
-> 1 Million Tower Points
-> Random Gift Bingo Ticket
’Looks like even the universe wants this scum dead. I guess I’ll get to it the moment I settle down in the academy,’ Kent smirked and retrieved one of the six necklaces Vexthra had given him.
"Put your blood on this and form a soul contract with it," Kent said, making Alina look at him strangely.
"Is... is that a soul item?" she asked curiously.
"Yes," Kent replied. He saw no reason to hide it. She was his woman now; the least he could do was protect her.
"And you’re giving it to me for free? Do you know how much one of these costs?" Alina asked, shocked. As an auction manager, she was well aware of the value of soul items.
Of course, she had never expected to own one herself, yet here she was, receiving one. Kent could only smile and say, "You don’t have to worry about the price."
He took her hand, pricked her thumb to draw blood, and dropped it onto the necklace. The contract was formed, and he placed it around her neck.
It felt surreal, but as she sensed the connection forming between her and the necklace, she seemed to accept it. Smiling, she hugged Kent tightly.
"Thank you," she whispered, burying her face in his chest. Kent simply patted her back, letting her have the moment she needed.
Of course, he went ahead and told her how the necklace worked.
Later, they dressed up, and Kent used his blink skill to leave the same way he had arrived. Alina, still smiling, left to take care of her affairs.
Since Kent had made her a promise, she resolved to do her best to live up to his expectations.
Right after Kent blinked outside the auction house, he began moving toward the southern part of the city. He was finally going to meet his servant, Jacob Ashland.
It had been weeks since the last time, he was sure.
Back then, Jacob had been captured by the men who worked for his father. But instead of killing him, they planned to sell him as a slave out of sheer greed.
Luckily for Jacob, Kent didn’t want to kill him, even though his family had captured Li Hua and were planning to use her for who knows what.
Long story short, Kent rescued him and offered him the chance to become his servant. After some internal struggles, Jacob accepted.
But then, his destiny took an unexpected turn when he received a True Name. It wasn’t just any ordinary True Name; it was that of the undying cockroach, Krex-Nithal.
Not that Jacob is aware he has a True Name. His True Name wouldn’t unlock until he raised his trust level with Kent to 80%.
Kent had planned on visiting him later.
However, something happened a few hours ago, and because of that, he decided to visit Jacob. His first servant had become a Root Saint, so Kent received a boost in his stats.
He hadn’t expected that. When he freed Jacob, the young man had shown no signs of continuing his cultivation. The first few weeks were spent lazing around.

He spent the 30,000 spirit stones Kent had given him recklessly. He seemed to have given up. However, a couple of weeks ago, something within him rebelled against the idea of surrendering and pushed him to pick himself up and do something meaningful with his life.

Thus, he began training and cultivating. By that time, he had already used up most of his money. With the little that remained, he rented a small apartment and threw himself into cultivating and training.

Before long, he became deeply engrossed in his efforts, and without realizing it, he finally accepted his role as Kent’s servant. Of course, he still hated Kent for taking his woman, but he had started to understand why things had unfolded the way they did.

He was nothing more than a puppet manipulated by his parents. He despised them, and now that they were dead, he was finally free. So, he trained harder, and before long, his Trust Level with Kent reached 50%.
A few hours ago, something remarkable happened—his cultivation base, which had been stuck at the Peak of the Root Grandmaster stage, finally broke through to the Root Saint stage.

Kent stopped 100 meters from the house and watched Jacob hack away at the training dummies he had bought. For several minutes, he observed him in silence. Then, with a soft smile, he stepped into the house.
"Good to see you’re doing better, Jacob," Kent said with a cute little smile. Jacob turned and looked at him but didn’t say anything.
Clearly, he still didn’t like him. But he had to admit, Kent had helped him, so, giving him the benefit of the doubt, he stopped what he was doing and faced him.
"What do you want?" Jacob asked.
Kent smirked, sensing the hostility in his tone. But he didn’t care—it’s not like Jacob could defeat him or anything.
"I just came to drop some things off before leaving. I know you still don’t trust me, but I hope you will in the future." Kent retrieved a pouch from his space ring.
"By the way, congratulations on becoming a Root Saint." He gave Jacob a nod of approval before tossing the pouch to him.

"Inside are 100 million spirit stones and a Soul Armor. Just put your blood on the gem in the armour, and it will be absorbed into your soul. To use it, just summon it, and it will appear around your body.
You can also imagine any type of clothing, and it will transform into it. Wear it at all times. I’ll come back or call you when I deem you worthy enough to be my true servant.
For now, use the money to buy what you need for your training." Kent smiled at Jacobs’s stunned expression and blinked away.
He didn’t need that much anyway, so giving him 100 million and one of the eight Soul Armors in his possession wasn’t a big deal.
If he needed more, he could just pop into the God Realm and get more.𝐟𝕣𝕖𝐞𝐰𝕖𝚋𝐧𝗼𝚟𝐞𝕝.𝗰𝐨𝐦

After leaving, Kent started moving toward the location of Vastport City. He could have used the transportation gate in Caprath City, but with four days left before going to the academy, he wanted to travel on foot.
So he set off.
However, halfway through the journey, he had to stop. Uncle Drew—now a Night Rider—appeared through a portal, along with two others, forcing Kent to halt.
He knew what was about to happen next. When the two figures behind Uncle Drew appeared, Kent received their True Names and understood how to complete their transformation.

chapters.title: Chapter 159: Awakening Ritual, The 2nd and 3rd Night Riders
paragraphs: "It’s been a while, Uncle Drew," Kent said with a cheerful smile.
Uncle Drew didn’t reply at first. He first turned back into his human form, flashed Kent a smile, and finally responded.
"Indeed, young master. I hope you’ve been well."
Kent nodded before turning his attention to the two figures behind Uncle Drew. By their appearances alone, he could tell one was female and the other male.
"They are the new additions to the ranks of the Night Riders," Uncle Drew explained. "It’s my job as the captain of the Night Riders to find those I can lead into the night."
Kent nodded in understanding. "I see. But I must first complete their transformations."
Uncle Drew nodded again, having brought them for that very reason.

Kent stepped toward Aria, who met his gaze from beneath her hood. She didn’t appear agitated or confused. Despite meeting Kent for the first time, she could sense that he was someone with immense authority over her.
Hyx, the former leader of the Dark Devil Church, was standing nearby. He now looked far more obedient.
Kent placed his index finger on her forehead and spoke a few words.
"By the silent vigil of the crescent moon, I call upon Lunaris Venator! Rise, Saden, and pierce the veil of shadows with your unerring light!"
As soon as Kent uttered those words, a crescent moon tattoo appeared on her forehead, and her body was suddenly enveloped in a green flame. Her clothing transformed, taking on a new form.
This time, it was mostly leather with tattered cloth lining certain parts. Her bow changed, becoming more bone-like, and a quiver made of an unknown material hung on her back.
Her Shadowmare also received upgrades, now bearing a metal armour-like coating around its vital areas.
When the transformation was complete, Kent felt his strength rise once again. It was a sign that Aria—now known as Saden—had officially joined the Night Riders.
"Welcome to the Legion, Aria—or should I call you Saden?" Kent asked.
"Aria was my past life. I would like to be called Saden from now on, Master," she replied politely, shifting into her human form.
A telepathic connection formed between her and Kent, meaning they can now communicate telepathically from anywhere.
"Then you shall be known from now onwards as Saden Nighthorn, the Luner Archeress." Her tattoo glowed a few times before dimming.
A swordsman and now an Archer has joined the night riders. His secret Army grows by the second. Kent was happy, so he quickly moved toward Hyx and did the same.
"From the depths where shadows reign, I summon Umbra Arcanis! Eryndor, command the night and awaken the spectral might of the Shadehoof bloodline!"
Similar changes occurred to him, but the most distinctive feature was the two horns that appeared on his forehead.
These transformations began when a tattoo of a shepherd’s staff appeared on his forehead. There was no doubt—Hyx, now known as Eryndor, was a summoner.

Before joining the Night Riders, summoning had been just a hobby for him. However, now he possessed the power to summon shadow beasts and could even tame creatures that would transform into shadow beasts the moment they were summoned.
"From now onwards, your name shall be Eryndor Shadehoof, the Shadow Summoner," Kent declared. Like Saden, he accepted his new name and officially became a Night Rider.
After everything was set, Uncle Drew provided Kent with a detailed rundown of the true identities of the two newest members of his secret army.
"Interesting. So, you were the one who ordered the 12 men to kill everyone in the Alderford mansion?" Kent asked with a smile.

Eryndor, formerly Hyx, visibly tensed. It was true—he had indeed sent men after his master. But that was his past self. He is now a changed man. His past self as the leader of the Dark Devil Church in Athea kingdom was somehow over.
"That was the past me, Master. I wouldn’t do that again," Eryndor said with a guilty expression. He was now in his human form.
"No need to tense up, Eryndor. I won’t bite. However, I do have a mission for you."
"You do?" He looked more relaxed now.

"Indeed. Since you’re high-ranking in the Dark Devil Church, you must have access to most of their information. I need that information. If possible, I want to know everything about the other branches they have in the other kingdoms," Kent said.
"I’ll get it done, Master, but it might take some time to gather everything you want," Eryndor replied, making Kent smile.
"Take your time. I don’t need it right away. However, since your mission is to retrieve the Atomic Divine Body, just tell them she was taken by the Hand," Kent proposed, and Eryndor nodded.
With Li Hua hidden inside the tower, no matter what they tried, they wouldn’t be able to track her. Kent knew better than to assume someone wouldn’t find a way to locate such a precious treasure.

After fine-tuning some more details with Eryndor, he left. He had quests that would gradually bring him closer to the head of the Dark Devil Church, but with Eryndor now under his command, progress would be much faster.

"Saden, do you need help with your revenge, or can you handle it on your own?" Kent turned to Saden, who burned with the desire for vengeance. Her friend—the one she called sister—had betrayed her, all because of petty jealousy over her beauty.
Saden wanted revenge, and she wanted it fast.
"I can do it alone, Master. I promise I’ll get things done quickly so I can return and serve you," Saden said, bowing deeply.
"No need to be so polite. Also, take your time with the revenge. It’s always better to savor it. As they say, revenge is best served cold," Kent said with a mischievous smile filled with dark intent.

Even Saden looked visibly shocked at the savagery she sensed from Kent. Of course, he seemed dangerous—he had every reason to be. After all, he had been murdered once and planned to settle that score someday.
"Then I will return when I’m done," Saden said.
"Don’t worry. Your captain and I have business to handle over the next few days, so take your time. He’ll call for you when he’s ready."
Saden left, taking her Night Rider form, which allowed her to traverse the realm of the night with ease.
"So, where is the master going?" Uncle Drew asked.

"I was on my way to Vastport City. From there, I’ll head to the sect with my master... By the way, my master would like to thank you in person, but we must first get to Vastport City," Kent said, making Uncle Drew nod.
The Shadowmare transformed into the carriage Kent had given him. It was the same carriage Jacob and his men had left in the Alderford Mansion.
"If the master keeps walking, it’ll take you two days to get there. With the carriage, we’ll get there in less than a day."
Kent nodded and got inside. He had already been walking for two days. A few seconds later, they started moving, heading toward Vastport City.
Uncle Drew could have used the power of the night to ride them through the night realm, where they would reach Vastport City in just a few minutes.
But that would defeat Kent’s purpose of wanting to catch some fresh air on his way to Vastport City.
Seventeen hours later, they arrived in Vastport City.

He’ll call for you when he’s ready."
Saden left, taking her Night Rider form, which allowed her to traverse the realm of the night with ease.
"So, where is the master going?" Uncle Drew asked.
"I was on my way to Vastport City.
From there, I’ll head to the sect with my master...
By the way, my master would like to thank you in person, but we must first get to Vastport City," Kent said, making Uncle Drew nod.
The Shadowmare transformed into the carriage Kent had given him.
It was the same carriage Jacob and his men had left in the Alderford Mansion.
"If the master keeps walking, it’ll take you two days to get there.
With the carriage, we’ll get there in less than a day."
Kent nodded and got inside.
He had already been walking for two days.
A few seconds later, they started moving, heading toward Vastport City.
Uncle Drew could have used the power of the night to ride them through the night realm, where they would reach Vastport City in just a few minutes.
But that would defeat Kent’s purpose of wanting to catch some fresh air on his way to Vastport City.
Seventeen hours later, they arrived in Vastport City.

chapters.title: Chapter 160: Vastport City
paragraphs: "So this is Vastport City, the famous capital of the Althea Kingdom," Kent said, standing beside Uncle Drew and overlooking the vast city with its towering walls and great buildings.
"It’s beautiful and well-protected," he added.
"Indeed. I was born and raised here, you know," Uncle Drew said, looking rather smug. Kent smiled but didn’t comment on his smugness. Instead, he asked a more personal question.
"Do you still have relatives here?"
Uncle Drew smiled and shook his head. "They are all dead. I was from a merchant family that met an unfortunate incident on our way to the Elven Empire. It was about 40 years ago, give or take."
Kent’s attention was drawn to the mention of a different race. "Sorry to hear that, but can I ask how it happened?"
Perhaps seeing the beautiful long ears on Nyxira, Elsa’s Assassin Soul Sentinel, he wanted to meet the elves and perhaps find himself a long ear or two.

"It’s an unfortunate incident with bandits and sea monsters. To get to the other continents, one must cross the Doom Seas. Of course, there are easier ways to get there, but it’s not cheap, so most just traverse the Doom Seas.

On our way, we were attacked by bandits, and, well, because of the chaos, the sea beasts used the opportunity to attack. I managed to escape, but up until now, I never knew how I escaped. It’s a bit bizarre now, thinking about it."
Kent didn’t say anything, but his mind raced with many conclusions, one of them being fate. Perhaps it was fate that played a hand.
It wouldn’t be a coincidence if it turned out that he survived so he could one day become Kael Duskbane, the captain of the Night Riders. It was no coincidence.
"So, have you been to any other continents?" Kent asked.
"Yes. I have been to the Elven continent, the Dwarven continent, and the Orc continent. But it was brief, as it was merely for business," Uncle Drew recalled, his expression thoughtful.
He was a very wealthy person back then, but after the incident on the Doom Seas, he had become a mere carriage driver in a low-level merchant family. That was indeed a fall from grace, one might say.
"Thank you for sharing this with me, but I have one last question." Kent smiled. "These sea beasts—how strong are they?"
A plan was already forming in his mind, and he wanted to satiate his curiosity. First, he craved adventure, and he could easily request a quest from the Universe Quest Pool.

Second, he needed bodies to create undead beings. That meant acquiring more bodies. If he could execute his plans effectively, he wouldn’t have to worry about the looming possibility of an apocalypse descending and ending all life.

"From what I know, just like on the surface, there are different species of beasts in the sea. Nobody knows how powerful they are, but many have said that the sea is the strongest force in this world.

According to several rumors, there have been over 15 sightings of peak Spirit Core Formation experts in the sea. And in case you don’t know, the Spirit Core Formation stage is the pinnacle of this world.
Beings at that level are considered unkillable."

Kent smiled, shaking his head. "Unkillable? I don’t think so. But 15 sightings certainly make them extremely dangerous. If they can afford to reveal 15 peak Spirit Core Formation experts, then there’s only one possibility...
They have more than 15 Spirit Core Formation experts, and as such, they want to show the surface world that they are not afraid of them."
Uncle Drew nodded.
"You know what, let’s forget about them for now. I want to know more about your new persona, Kael Duskbane."
Kent’s curiosity had already been satiated, so his next move was to commit himself to taking his swordsmanship to a higher level, one where he could roam freely.
The current him was strong, but he was not invincible. Any mistake or slip-up could land him in hot water. For now, he wanted to assess all of his strengths.
He and Uncle Drew spent the next few hours talking about the Night Riders. Of course, he never expected to learn their full backstory, so he only asked about what Uncle Drew knew.
But he was disappointed to find out that Uncle Drew knew very little. From what he gathered, it seemed the Night Riders had a long legacy, one that, at some point, wreaked havoc across the universe.
Uncle Drew told him that all Night Riders have a powerful connection to the underworld. And it’s not the underworld, one might think—it’s the real underworld, where the 13 levels of hell exist.
The Night Riders were like a legion that once rose from the depths of hell—even beyond the 13th level. They rose and scorched the night with their fury.

While Uncle Drew was speaking, Kent could swear he experienced a state of déjà vu, as though he had been there. The feeling was one of kinship, the kind you only get from doing something that transcends common sense.
This made him want to understand more about the origin of the Night Riders. He wanted to understand their power, nature, and innate ability to ride the night into battle.
However, in the end, he only learned a little. But even that little told him he might have just inherited the strongest underworld army the universe has ever known.
After a few more conversations, they entered the city and were greeted by the bustling sight of people moving to and fro, going about their business.
Kent quickly found an inn, rented a private room, and immediately entered the tower. A few minutes later, he returned with Saintess Selene, who sincerely thanked Uncle Drew for saving her life.
After that, he sent her back inside the tower and took Uncle Drew out. Kent chose to use the day he had to go around the city and buy some ingredients.
He was still 30 Tier 2 pills short of completing the second requirement of the quest he had received, which he must finish before officially becoming a Pill Grandmaster.
After wandering the city for a couple of hours, Kent and Uncle Drew stopped in front of a herb store called [The Alchemist’s Dream.]
It was quite large, and without even entering, Kent could already sense its reputation by using his Enchanted Eyes to appraise it.
Essentially, [The Alchemist’s Dream] was the largest alchemy shop in the entire kingdom. It was the oldest, and the only store where most herbs one might need could be found.

Through his appraisal, Kent also learned that, across the human continent, [The Alchemist’s Dream] was the second-largest alchemy store. Alchemists from various cities and kingdoms came here to buy and sell.
In fact, just standing outside confirmed its reputation was well-deserved.

The number of carriages parked or coming and going spoke volumes. Thankfully, Kent wasn’t in an ordinary carriage himself. Uncle Drew had done an excellent job spending the spirit stones Kent had given him.
Their carriage looked majestic.
"Uncle Drew, I’ll be gone for a few hours, maybe," Kent said.
"I’ll wait here for the young master," Uncle Drew replied, making Kent nod before he started walking inside. He just wanted to buy some herbs.
"Stop there, show some identification..." Of course, he was stopped before he could enter.

chapters.title: Chapter 161: The Alchemist Dream
paragraphs: Kent was stopped before he could enter the store. Of course, he had expected that, considering he was a nobody at the moment.
He didn’t even have any form of identification, which, in this context, would require proof of whether he belonged to a powerful family or not.
Alternatively, it could show that he held a status that qualified him to enter the store.𝕗𝐫𝚎𝗲𝘄𝐞𝕓𝐧𝕠𝘃𝕖𝐥.𝐜𝚘𝚖
[The Alchemist’s Dream] was a highly reputable establishment offering various services, so the last thing they wanted was for some no-name individual to disrupt their business.
"I’m sorry, but I don’t have any identification..." Kent said, sounding as polite as he could manage.
They always say the wicked are often the most respectful. You only see their true colors when they’re angry...
"Without any identification, you can’t enter," the guard who had stopped him said, showing no signs of hostility. This unexpected politeness made Kent’s opinion of the store rise slightly.
"Although I don’t have identification, I am an alchemist and would love to enter this magnificent herb haven to purchase some herbs. Please, is there no other way for me to gain entry?" Kent asked.
"Yeah, well, if you are an Alchemist, then I am a Sage Alchemist..." Of course, just because one guard was respectful doesn’t mean all of them are.
Kent didn’t bother to look at the new guard, who seemed to have a lot of time on his hands, and chose to butt into his conversation with the first guard.
"Surely, there are other ways for me to enter this store. If there are any, I would like to explore them." Kent was no fool.
He may be from Earth, but he knew there were many ways to do things in this life.

Take Earth, for example: aside from using your CV to get a job, there are many backdoors one can explore to land a paying job. Kent knew that no matter the world he was in, provided there were living creatures, backdoors would never close.
As expected, the first guard, who seemed to like the tone Kent was using, smiled. He looked at the second guard, who was about to explode, and gave him a look. This made him calm down a bit.

"If this young Alchemist wants to enter, he must donate to the cause of this noble store. I believe a couple of thousand spirit stones will go a long way," the first guard said, making the second guard nod with a sudden glint in his eyes.
Kent just smiled and retrieved a pouch discreetly.
There were a lot of people going in and out, so the chances of somebody noticing what was happening were very high.
"Since we all want this noble store to keep growing, I would love to donate, of course," he said, handing the pouch to the first guard as he began walking into the store.
Once Kent left, the guard peeked inside. Thanks to the enchantment on the pouch, he immediately counted the amount it housed.
He froze and nearly dropped the pouch. Thankfully, he composed himself and turned to the second guard.
"How much?" the second guard asked.
"500,000," the first guard replied, making the second guard grin from ear to ear. They quickly moved away and shared the amount among themselves.

Of course, as they say, it’s not every day you meet your destiny changer, and in this case, Kent had blessed them with a million. But the wicked will always play the game of deceit... After all, there is nothing noble about taking a bribe.

Kent, who had managed to step inside the store, was blown away by the majestic-looking shelves filled with herbs that seemed to have been purposely placed in formations meant to keep them fresh for a long time.
"Welcome to the Alchemist’s Dream. How can I be of service, young alchemist?" Just as Kent was marveling at the display, a young lady about his age, dressed in a green alchemy robe, spoke to him.
Kent looked back at her and asked, "How do you know I am an alchemist?"

Of course, it was foolish to ask that, considering he was standing in a space filled with alchemists. But then again, he could just as easily be some random young master looking to buy a rare herb for his family.
"The look in your eyes shows you are someone who appreciates the craft. Not everyone your age would have such a dazed look in their eyes if they weren’t an alchemist," the lady said with a smile.

Kent smiled back, making his handsome features even more noticeable. Of course, he wasn’t looking to cause a scene, so he quickly stopped smiling and said, "Then, since this young miss has uncovered my hidden obsession, may I trouble her to show me where I can find some Tier 2 herbs? I prefer herbs that can be used for poison pills."
The lady arched an eyebrow at his request. "Poison pills... Those are expensive, even at Tier 2. But I have to ask—why would a young alchemist like yourself choose to delve into poison pill making?"
Kent smiled again. "Well, what can I say? Everyone has their quirks, I guess. But I didn’t choose poison pills out of an obsession. I just like to keep my survival chances open."
The lady seemed to understand what he meant. With poison pills, he could indeed increase his chances of surviving even the most harrowing situations.
Then again, if he was looking to make money, poison pills also sold quite well. He could earn a fortune selling poison pills, regardless of their tier.
No matter how strong a person was, they would inevitably be affected by a poison pill, even if only for a few seconds—possibly giving him a chance to escape if necessary.
"Follow me," the lady said, leading him to the section where the poison herbs were displayed. Along the way, she struck up a conversation, causing Kent’s opinion of her to improve slightly.
"So, from what I can tell, you are a Pill Master. I want to know—do you plan on joining the Pill Master competition happening less than three months from now?"
"Of course. I want to measure myself against the young and brightest of this kingdom and see where I stand," Kent said in a polite tone, which made the lady give him a strange look.
She sensed some mocking undertone in his words, but she couldn’t quite figure out where the mockery was directed.
However, she didn’t comment on it. Instead, she asked something else.
"May I know which noble family you are from? The store offers discounts for certain families, so that could go a long way in reducing the cost of your purchases."
Kent smiled inwardly. He knew everything she had just said was nonsense. Any discount would have been clearly stated when he got to the counter to pay for his goods.

It was obvious to him that the lady was fishing for information about his background. While she appeared young, Kent knew she was old in the ways of alchemy. His enchanted eyes revealed her true identity as a Pill Grandmaster and a Root Great Sage.
She was using a pill to disguise herself and suppress her cultivation base. But Kent didn’t care; he was only here to buy herbs.
"I’m sorry to disappoint, but I’m not from any noble family. And by the way, you can just call me Kent," he said, keeping his tone neutral.

chapters.title: Chapter 162: Impulse Buying
paragraphs: The lady stared back at Kent as though scrutinizing him to determine whether what he said was true. After an intense 30 seconds of staring, she seemed to find her answer, her expression shifting as if she had just discovered a rare gem.
Kent noticed the look in her eyes and immediately understood what she was thinking. Without hesitation, he dismissed any direction she might want to take.
"Being part of a noble or merchant family is not something I’m interested in. They’re all about scheming and backstabbing."
The lady seemed to grasp Kent’s point and decided to back off. However, that doesn’t mean she completely dismissed the idea.
"But of course," she replied, choosing not to press further. Instead, she led him to the section of the store that housed the poison-type herbs.

"While you may not like the idea of joining a noble or merchant family, you should know that they come with amazing benefits and protection. However, as great as that might sound, showing exceptional skill during the competition has its downsides," the lady explained, her tone neutral and unreadable.
"How so?" Kent asked.
"For starters, the noble and merchant families are highly competitive. They always strive to have the best of everything. If you become the top ranker in the competition, they’ll try to recruit you.
But if you refuse, they won’t take it kindly. They may resort to nefarious methods to get their way. In short, if they can’t have you, then nobody else can," she warned.
Kent nodded with a thoughtful expression.

The last thing he wanted was to get entangled with these noble families. But since they seemed to have a problem with his unwillingness to join them, the best he could do was unleash an army of battle dolls on them.
And if that wasn’t enough? Well, he was now a [Create Necromancer], capable of far more than just summoning battle dolls.

With that thought lingering in his mind, Kent continued browsing through the store, carefully checking and selecting the herbs he needed while keeping an eye out for new ones to add to his collection.
Money wasn’t an issue for him.

"You seem to be picking a lot. Do you know the store has a policy that prohibits returning herbs to the shelves after they’ve been picked?" the lady remarked, eyeing the stack of herbs Kent had gathered.
"Don’t worry, I planned on buying all of this," Kent smiled, continuing to select herbs.
"Are you one of those?" the lady asked thoughtfully.
"One of who?" Kent replied.
"You know, those impulse buyers," she smiled as she said it. Kent smiled back and picked four herbs: Bloodthorn Vines, Crimsonbell Flowers, Fevermoss, and Blightcap Spores.

"I assure you, I’m not an impulse buyer. I just like impulse buying. The two are completely different, by the way." Kent wasn’t sure if he had just made a fool of himself or if it actually made sense.
The lady glanced at the four herbs in his hand and asked, "Since you’re not an impulse buyer, why don’t you tell me what these four herbs are used for?"

The first man paled upon hearing that. They knew who that old witch was and what she could do to people. In fact, among the Seven Pill Saints, she was regarded as the most dangerous of them all.
It wasn’t because she was the best.
No.

It was more like she was dangerous. She specialized in making poisons, so when they called her a monster, she truly deserved the title. Her pills were some of the most potent poisons this continent has ever seen.
People who recognized her seemed to want to distance themselves from where the young disciple of the wicked Pill Saint stood.

One time, a certain merchant family offended the old witch, who, overnight, poisoned the entire family, leaving them in agonizing pain for three whole months. Both old and young, she showed no remorse.
Had it not been for the king stepping in, she would have left them like that for who knows how long. So because of this, in the four kingdoms, nobody wanted to mess with her or anyone related to her.
They feared her like a plague. If possible, they all wanted to run outside first until she left before returning. Disciple or the real deal, they wouldn’t want to test their luck.
"I am sorry, miss, but this herb has been accounted for by this young man," the counter lady said, pointing at Kent.

The young disciple lady turned and stared at Kent with eyes filled with disdain and arrogance. Right now, she felt like she was invincible—and she was. Despite being inside the most powerful store in Althea Kingdom, she indeed felt untouchable, thanks to her master.
However, today, in the eyes of the Chaos Dragon, she was a nobody. And he made sure she knew that.

"Stop looking at me with those eyes. No matter who you are, whether the daughter of the king or the princess of the demon empire, this herb won’t be given to you today or ever. So you can just run along," Kent spoke, and jaws dropped.

chapters.title: Chapter 163: Who cares about your master?
paragraphs: The moment Kent’s words left his mouth, everyone paled. It was as if doom had descended upon them, which was ironic considering the one who spoke the words appeared rather calm.
But, of course, they had every reason to react that way, knowing what they knew.
Kent had just disrespected the only disciple of the Old Wicked Witch. That was an offense no one would be foolish enough to commit.

Even the Pill Grandmaster in disguise, who had escorted him through the store, took a few steps away from him, increasing the distance. She knew it would be wiser to save her own neck than to protect some random, handsome man she had been trying to recruit into her family.
"What did you just say?" the disciple asked, glaring dangerously at Kent.

"I don’t repeat myself, but since you can’t hear well, listen closely. This herb was found and picked by me. I won’t hand it over to you just because of your status or the family you’re from. So, you can run along."
"You... Do you know who I am? Do you know who my master is?" the disciple demanded, pointing at Kent with her left hand.
"Bitch, you better take that finger out of my face before I cut it off. Don’t you know it’s disrespectful to point at people?" Kent glared at her and swatted her hand away.
"And who cares about your master?" His words once again made everyone look at him strangely. In their minds, Kent was already a dead man.
"You bastard! Do you think you can disrespect my master and get away with it? I won’t let this slide." She retrieved a token from her space ring and presented it to the counter lady.
The moment the lady’s eyes landed on it, her face turned pale. "That..."
"Yes, this is the token of a Pill Saint. I advise you not to go against it, or you already know the repercussions," the disciple sneered, casting a sidelong glance at Kent.
"I’m sorry, young man, but the store cannot oppose the authority of one of the Pill Saints," the counter lady said, her voice laced with hesitation.
Kent frowned. He could tell she wouldn’t budge—her survival depended on avoiding the wrath of the token’s owner.
Kent understood the ranks of alchemists, and he knew a Pill Saint was indeed someone no one should offend. Yet, seeing the young disciple wielding the badge to get her way filled him with anger.
For some reason, watching someone misuse an item of such significance, belonging to another alchemist, made him want to light his pill flame and scorch her arrogant face.
Perhaps it was the pride of an alchemist stirring within him.
Kent smirked and turned to the counter lady.
"I understand. I won’t put you in a difficult position."
He then faced the disciple.
"I assume that badge belongs to your master, correct?"

The young lady nodded smugly. "Yes, and you should know better than to go against it. I may forgive your earlier remarks, but any further defiance and your entire family will feel the wrath of the Wicked Poison Witch."

"Tsk." Kent chuckled, then turned back to the counter lady. "Kindly tally my total, including the Dreamshade Flower. If the owner of the badge has an issue, direct her to the Divine Palace Sect. I will handle it."
Kent’s tone was firm and unwavering. He had no intention of conceding to anyone, no matter who the badge belonged to. Even if she held the power to take his life, she wouldn’t intimidate him.
He turned back to the young disciple, whose face now bore a shocked expression.

"You can tell your master to respect the laws of alchemy. Letting you wield her badge to fool around is plain disgusting. Tell her to learn the rules. If she refuses, she’s welcome to find me—I’ll gladly help her out."
With that, he waited as the counter lady, clearly relieved by Kent’s arrogance, quickly finalized the total. She had no desire to linger in the tense atmosphere.
"That will be 930,000 spirit stones," she said.
Kent retrieved a pouch containing the spirit stones and handed it to her. He cast one last look at the disciple, taking the pouch of herbs.
"If you want the authority of a Pill Saint, then become a Pill Saint. Don’t use someone else’s badge to intimidate others."
He left without paying any attention to the strange looks aimed his way. He had just disrespected the badge of a Pill Saint, but he didn’t care.
Everyone watched him leave like a ghost. It was only after Kent left the store that people started to recover and began to whisper.
They all began asking themselves a series of questions, with a few already mourning Kent’s inevitable clash with the Wicked Poison Witch.
They knew that no matter the position Kent held in the academy, they wouldn’t dare cross the Wicked Poison Witch for him. Nobody, not even the kings, would do that.

The truth of the matter was that the Seven Pill Saints were the most powerful people the kingdoms had. Of course, there were strong cultivators the kingdoms needed, but these alchemists controlled the market with their pills.

So for a disciple of one of them to be humiliated like that—well, in fact, the Alchemist Dream might catch some stray bullets if the young lady, who was left disappointed, angry, and nearly bursting into flames, chose to use her anger to complain to her master.
Once Kent left, he and Uncle Drew returned to the inn he had hired. There, Kent took him inside the Legion Tower, and together, they managed to create the perfect barracks for the Night Riders.

Of course, Uncle Drew had always wanted to stay inside the realm of the Night. Still, since they also cultivate like normal beings, Kent granted him the authority to allow himself and anyone in his legion to enter the tower.
It was like an admin privilege, and now, Uncle Drew had full access to the Legion Tower.
"So, where would you be going next, Young Master?" Uncle Drew asked.

"From here, I am going straight to the academy with my master, where I will be staying for a while. Of course, I will occasionally go to places outside the academy, so if I need help, I will reach out.
But for now, just find that Turyn guy and use the talisman I gave you to send him to me. I’ll take care of the rest," Kent replied, and Uncle Drew nodded.

Kent had tasked him and Saden with capturing the bastard who had hurt his woman when she was just 18. He gave him an item that would directly transport Turyn to the Tower Prison, where Kent planned to torture him for a month before sending him to Alina.
If necessary, he intended to make Turyn suffer so severely that he would beg for death instead.
After eating together, Uncle Drew left and headed toward Varyndor, the kingdom where the Miller family resided.
Meanwhile, Kent used the time difference inside the tower to begin concocting pills. In his eyes, if things took an unexpected turn, humanity would simply lose a Pill Saint.
After all, he, in a way, had his own Pandora’s box... If the Pill Saint refused to listen to reason, it would just result in Kent gaining a Soul-Spirit and a powerful dead body in the coming days.

chapters.title: Chapter 164: I Am Ready, Kent
paragraphs: [Ironpeak City]

Annabelle was the most feared young lady in the entire Kyrrith Kingdom. It was also the strongest kingdom on the human continent, so for someone to be feared throughout this kingdom meant she was feared across the whole human continent.
The reason was simple.
Annabelle was no ordinary young lady. She was the disciple of one of the seven Saint Alchemists on the continent.
In fact, her master’s status was such that it could be said Annabelle was the disciple of the most wicked righteous person on the entire human continent.

Pill Saint Riva, also known as the Wicked Poison Witch, was feared by all, as was her disciple. However, today, someone had not only disrespected Annabelle but also dishonoured the badge that belonged to her master, a grave offence.

Annabelle, who had been disgraced by Kent, left the Althea Kingdom fuming, her face set in a scowl, as she made her way back to her master, who was currently working on creating a powerful new recipe for a Tier 7 pill.
"Master, I need revenge!" Annabelle cried as she ran into her master’s house upon her arrival.

Her master, the woman in question, didn’t look very old. However, perhaps due to her practice, her appearance was far from pleasant. Dark circles shadowed her eyes, and her fingertips were stained black, likely from poison or something equally sinister.
She had short hair, and were it not for her demented nature, she might have attracted men with the prominence of her chest and the curve of her hips. She is packing on both fronts.
"What happened?" Pill Saint Riva asked.

"Some bastard bought the Dreamshade Flower I needed, and when I asked for it back, he outright insulted me and you. He said that no matter who I am or what my status is, he wouldn’t give me the herb." Annabelle clenched her fists, her frustration was evident.
"Even after I used your badge, he didn’t budge. He even told me to tell you to learn the laws of alchemy and said that if you don’t know them, feel free to find him—he’ll teach you."
"What... Who the hell is he to think he can tell me what to do?" Pill Saint Riva shouted, abruptly standing up from her work.
"Do you know his name or where he’s from?" she asked sharply.
"He said he’s from the Divine Palace Sect," Annabelle replied, her frown unwavering.
"I see. Go and finish your assignment. The moment I’m done with this, we’ll see who will be teaching whom the laws of alchemy."
Annabelle nodded and hugged her master, burying her face between the woman’s ample bosom. Pill Saint Riva, who had always indulged her disciple, gently patted her head.
"Don’t worry. We’ll be getting the herb back."
With that reassurance, Annabelle ran off to her apartment, leaving Pill Saint Riva alone, a deep frown now etched on her face.
"The laws of alchemy..." she muttered, a sense of foreboding settling over her.
She is an alchemist, and the laws of Alchemy are something nobody—not even the Pill God—can go against. Of course, in a medium world like this, those laws are not widely known.
However, the fact that she gave her alchemy badge to her disciple was a great offence. If the laws were to be enforced, it would result in her losing her ranking for 200 years.
This means that for 200 years, she wouldn’t be known as a Pill Saint, nor could she enjoy the privilege of entering places reserved exclusively for Pill Saints.
The rules are very strict, and because of this, she knew that if this unknown youngster were to somehow make these laws known, she would be in hot water.
"He must be taken care of," she muttered before returning to her work.
In a week’s time, she would be heading to the Althea Kingdom, specifically to the Divine Palace Sect, where she planned to use her authority to get her way.

Meanwhile, while this master and disciple duo were making plans to go after Kent, the young man in question had just concocted the last pill, achieving the threshold of 60 Tier 1 pills and 60 Tier 2 pills.
These are two out of the four requirements to become a Pill Grandmaster. In a way, he had just completed these requirements and was now left with the final two.𝒇𝒓𝒆𝒆𝙬𝒆𝒃𝓷𝒐𝓿𝙚𝙡.𝒄𝓸𝒎

"The Tier 3 pill recipe has now been purchased, and I have the ingredients. However, I need to wait a few days to practice my flame technique and become more confident in my ability to concoct a Tier 3 pill.
I have six portions of the ingredients, so I won’t fail."
Kent stood up and entered a small house he had spent 20,000 Tower Points to build inside the Alchemy Tower. It contained a bath where he quickly freshened up.
He had already spent six days inside the tower, but only six hours had passed outside. That meant he still had 18 hours outside before he and his master departed for the academy.

Of course, this also meant he had 18 days inside the tower to do whatever he wanted. While he knew what he wanted to do, instead of heading to the Harem Tower, he first went to Tower City, where Gaia, Akira, Li Hua, and the three Soul Sentinels were now living.
They had grown much closer to the three lolis. Li Hua, in particular, had become close with Nyxira, the elf assassin who was also the strongest of the three Soul Sentinels under Elsa.
Li Hua wanted Nyxira to teach her how to fight, using the excuse that she wanted to avenge her grandmother.
Because of this, Gaia contacted Kent to let him know the little human child was still traumatized by the events that had led to her master’s death.

Kent spent two days with her, knowing it wouldn’t be enough to completely address her trauma. However, he also knew she wouldn’t stop pursuing vengeance, so he arranged for Li Hua to become Nyxira’s disciple.

This way, Nyxira could use their relationship to stall her until she came of age. Nonetheless, even without much formal teaching, Nyxira planned to teach her some dagger techniques to make her feel empowered.
Li Hua might be a child, but after the events that led to her grandmother’s death, she changed completely.
After leaving that place, Kent went to the Tower Store, where he purchased items he planned to use against the Pill Saint in case she came looking for trouble.
Right now, all he needed was more Tower Points to acquire some of the best treasures the universe had to offer.
He wants to make sure he is always prepared for danger.
If she came in peace, things would remain peaceful. Otherwise, chaos would ensue.
After leaving the Tower store, he entered the Harem Tower. He appeared inside the Love Garden, knowing the four ladies were in the pool.
However, the moment he appeared, he saw his master sitting in a lotus posture with her eyes closed. Kent sensed that she had become a Root Great Sage and had even stabilized her cultivation base.
Kent smiled and then sat down behind her. After an hour, she opened her eyes and turned to him.

"Congrats, Master. You are now a Root Great Sage," Kent said with a smile, making his master smile as well. After smiling, she looked into his eyes for a whole minute until she finally said the magic words.
"I am ready, Kent."

She wanted in on that.

[Don’t worry, you’ll be descending soon.
For now, just give me two months tops.]
"Okay, my love.
Now, hurry up and add my new sister.
I can’t wait to turn her into a monster with the sword."
Kent smiled and gave Gaia the go-ahead.
Immediately, he felt the connection form between him and his master.

chapters.title: Chapter 169: The Harem Council
paragraphs: The moment Vexthra’s voice sounded in Saintess Selene’s head, her body stiffened, a shocked expression painting her face.
"Told ya," Kent said with a smile.

Saintess Selene was indeed shocked. For a moment, she thought Kent was just messing with her when he said he had a goddess as a wife; however, the moment the voice entered her mind, she got her answer.
"Hello, are you there?" Vexthra spoke again. "I know this is shocking, but whatever that bastard said is true. I am his first wife, and I am also a goddess... Your new sister."

Saintess Selene gulped and then used the connection to answer, fully realizing this was happening. As much as she wanted to think this was just a dream, she knew this was reality, and it was unfolding right in front of her.
"Nice meeting you. I am Selene," she replied, bringing a smile to Vexthra’s face. Vexthra immediately linked her up with the rest of her sisters.
"Welcome, Big Sister Selene," Unity greeted warmly, followed by Lilian and Elsa. By the time the three were done, Selene knew this wasn’t a dream at all.
"Now that we’ve all introduced ourselves, how about we get down to business?" Vexthra said, drawing the attention of the three ladies and their newly added sister.
Kent watched the expression on Selene’s face and smiled. He knew Vexthra was handling things in her way, so he simply leaned back and let her finish.
"Tell us, Sister Selene, what has Kent told you so far?"
Selene, understanding their question, went ahead and shared what Kent had explained about dual cultivation. She didn’t mention anything about Kent being a dragon, assuming they already knew.
"So, you already know that in the future, more ladies will be joining us, right? Are you fine with that?" Vexthra asked.
"I don’t mind, and I am happy with the decision to become his woman," she said, trying to sound bold.
The four ladies smiled, knowing she was just putting on a brave front. Of course, they had all been like her just a few weeks ago, so it was normal.

"Then you should also know that since you are the strongest so far, you will have to do more and help him raise his cultivation base. This means you will have to have more sex with your beloved disciple,"
Vexthra said, intentionally using the master-disciple relationship between Selene and Kent to make her blush—and it worked.
"Now that we’ve settled that, how about we catch her up on our plan?" Lilian suggested, knowing this was one of the main reasons they had formed this council.
Selene, sensing the shift in tone, knew it was time to focus on something important, so she chose to listen. It felt strange, but she knew it would soon become normal.

"So, our plan is simple. Since we are now Kent’s women, we plan to find more beautiful and capable ladies for him. Of course, they don’t have to be stronger than him, but if they are, that’s fine, too.
It will even be better if they are much stronger than him.
The reason I’m saying this is because of a certain aspect of Kent. It was a secret at first, but he gave me the go-ahead, so I want to share it.

According to Kent, when he adds new women, he receives certain benefits from us. First, he gains a random skill from our arsenal. Second, he gets a boost in his stats. Most importantly, he receives a portion of the spiritual energy we absorb during cultivation.

This means that if there are dozens of us, the more we cultivate, the stronger he gets. That’s why I came up with this plan and formed this council. We’re here to ensure our man grows stronger and faster."
Vexthra’s words made the four ladies’ eyes widen. Selene, of course, glanced at the sleeping Kent, and for a moment, she wanted to punch him.
However, she stopped when Vexthra spoke again.
"I know this may sound like he’s using us, but in truth, we are actually the ones who will benefit the most. If you don’t believe me, why don’t you all ask Elsa what happened to her?"
Elsa smiled and decided to share her story.
"When Kent added me to the harem, I triggered a True Name. Of course, I had no idea what that was, but after talking to Big Sister, I learned it was something only Kent could grant.
Long story short, when Kent invoked this True Name, I changed. Everything about me changed—even my body was reborn. From that, I became a new person.
Now, I have a strong connection to the soul and am in the process of awakening half of my bloodline. Even without it, I’m incredibly powerful now, and it’s all thanks to Kent.

He not only changed my life but, by loving me, he also changed my destiny. Now, I can boldly say that giving him a part of our cultivation or even a piece of our soul doesn’t compare to the reward he gave me."
Vexthra continued.
"He told me we will all eventually receive True Names and unlock our hidden potentials. So, while you may think this is a one-sided benefit, think again.
For now, we can only wait for him to grant us True Names but know that the moment we accepted the decision to become his woman, our destinies were bound to change.
Kent is someone even I can’t compare to—and I am a goddess."
The past weeks had been about Vexthra thinking about a lot of things. In fact, she had started to think that maybe, when she received the tower for safekeeping, that was when she truly became his.
Even she began to wonder if Kent finding himself inside the realm of hatred and resentment wasn’t by accident. Because of this, she was convinced that Kent was someone she couldn’t even look down on.

"So, since we all know there is a great reward waiting for us, we should also do our best to love our man and make him very happy." The four ladies nodded, knowing that what Vexthra said was indeed true.

Even Saintess Selene was starting to see the positive side of things. First, she noticed how much more lively her life had become since meeting Kent. Now, she had four sisters, and one of them was even a goddess. How awesome was that?
She felt happy inwardly.
"So, Sister Selene, do you regret becoming his woman?" Vexthra asked.
"No. I am happy, and I’m even planning to make my sister one of his women soon," she replied with a smile, making the four ladies smile as well.
"Nice one. Now, since you are one of us, it’s time for me to create a new cultivation technique for you."
They continued their chat for hours while Vexthra worked on her cultivation technique.

While this was happening, Kent was busy examining the crazy skill he had received from Selene. In fact, he wasn’t sure how to perceive this new skill. It felt as though the universe had chosen to reward him through Selene.
He knew for a fact that his master didn’t have this skill, so it seemed only natural that perhaps the universe had played a hand in this.
And he was right. The universe had indeed played a hand in this. He had, once again, become a monster who would soon rule this world...
