chapters.title: Chapter 189: Heaven Ascendence Sword Path
paragraphs: Ten hours had passed since Kent entered the tower to recover. Meanwhile, inside the tower, ten days had gone by. Having completed his body tempering, Kent was now in the Harem Tower eating strawberries.
Akira and Gaia were present, using a strand of their consciousness.
Kent strolled through the Harem Tower for a few hours before finally returning to the Alchemy Tower, where he spent a day meditating.
"The master has received the fifth sword path. Does the master want to create a space for it, like with the Genesis Path?" Gaia asked, gazing intently at Kent.
Kent could tell she was up to no good, but he also knew that whatever she was planning was likely something he wanted.
Kent didn’t immediately reply. He first took out the Heaven Ascendence Sword Path manual, and from just a few pages, he could tell it was different from his.

"This is the fifth sword path, master. It would look different from yours. In fact, yours would be different from the others, considering it’s the first true path, and it was through that the others were made," Gaia explained.
Kent nodded.
"So, would this path lead to the pinnacle of the sword path?" Kent asked.
"Of course. It’s a very powerful sword path. If your master manages to walk it well, she will undoubtedly become incredibly monstrous with the sword.
Luckily for her, she has the lightning element, which is a must for this path of the sword."
Kent nodded and then took out a true name token, one of the rewards he had earned from the quest. The other was 1 million Tower points, which he planned on using in the coming days.
After his talk with the Spear Saintess, he had a reality check, and now, he wanted nothing more than to avoid falling into the trap of any shameless powerhouse who simply couldn’t accept a loss.
He planned on giving Unity a True name, considering she is the only one among his ladies with low talent...well, that was what he thought.

"Akira, I want you to spend the next few days going through the Tower store and look for treasures that will have the most impact, even against those realms above me," Kent said before turning to Gaia.
Akira runs off, ready to get useful...
"Let’s create a path for the Heaven Ascendence Sword Path inside the Sword Tower," Kent instructed.
Gaia nodded and then made some calculations with her finger. Keny could only smile, knowing what was coming next...Li Hua has corrupted the tower with her greed for money.
"That will cost 400 thousand tower points. Since I know you are all about perfection, I plan on making the most perfect sword path for your master," Gaia said, and Kent could only shake his head.
He expected things to be much more expensive, but it seems he was wrong.
"Go ahead," Kent gave her the go-ahead.
At the same time, he felt his connection to the sword tower severed. He didn’t panic and just went about his meditation. He now had nothing to do...
Well, he still had to concoct a Tier 3 perfect pill, but he wanted to first increase his understanding of his flame control technique.
Thankfully, his mind was getting stronger as he practised the sword mind, so he was using his mind to learn it first.
Naturally, that shouldn’t be possible for someone at his level.
However, since he started practising sword mind from the moment he began walking the path of cultivation, he could now practice and master techniques theoretically before actively using them.
So, he resumed his meditation, and for three straight days, he sat there meditating.
On the fourth day, he felt his connection to the sword tower form again, making him stop the meditation and choose to explore what Gaia had cooked up.
When he arrived inside the sword tower, he could tell something was different or something else had been added. A couple of somethings, actually...
"I initially wanted to add it to your domain, but that would make it too complex, so I created a pocket dimension inside the sword tower where her separate training space was built.
You can use that portal to enter."
Kent nodded and walked toward the portal, stopping right when he was in front of it.
"That is some powerful lightning energy coming from inside," Kent said, looking into the portal.
"This is a path of the sword. You entering shouldn’t even be allowed since you wouldn’t be walking that path. For now, you can only enter because of your Tower Master authority," Gaia said.
Kent nodded and entered. The moment he appeared inside the domain of the Heaven Ascendence Sword Path, his hair stood on end.
It was a world filled with lightning. Everything was lightning, and it kept rumbling every now and then. He looked all around, but all he could see was lightning.
"This is as far as you can go, unless you want to walk the Heaven Ascendence Sword Path. If not, you cannot proceed forward. However, I will let you see a few things."

Kent nodded. All he could see was lightning, but when Gaia waved her hand, the lightning cleared, and he could see a large sword, similar to his, embedded at the centre of the domain. It had lightning dancing around it.

"Your master would first have to rebuild her foundation, which means she will start from the beginner stage again. However, since she is currently a Sword Saint, it wouldn’t take her more than a year to return to her current stage.
I created this sword from the Heaven Ascendence Sword Path, called [Heavens Ascendence Foundation Sword].
Do you see those sword markings on it? She must follow those steps, comprehending them through meditation and practice."
"This is great then. With the time difference in the tower, she can rebuild her path within a month or even less," Kent smiled.
"Yes. And also, once she is done rebuilding her foundation, the next path will show itself, just like how yours appeared."
Kent looked around, but for now, all he could see was the sword and a stone-like platform where she would sit to comprehend the sword.
Kent was sure the stone would have some enchantments, but he wasn’t about to accidentally compromise the reward he had made for his woman by getting curious.
"Thank you, Gaia. This is the best."
Gaia smiled. "This is the master’s effort... Without the master completing the quest, none of this would be possible."
Kent smiled and then chose to leave the pocket domain. He would let his master come here and start comprehending this path, which would, without a doubt, one day help her rise to the pinnacle.
"Gaia, I have been meaning to ask, but are there paths for the other weapons and professions? Also, can two people walk the same path?" Kent asked.

"Yes. There are other paths for other weapons and professions. Everything has a path. However, obtaining them is not easy. Take this fifth sword path, for example. You received it easily only because of the Quest Pool.

In case the master doesn’t know, there are 21 Primordial paths in the sword path, of which yours and the fifth are two of the 21. However, after that Primordial era, many swordsmen rose and fell. Some managed to rise to the pinnacle.
These other paths are the Primitive paths. Though powerful, they pale compared to the Primordial paths.
This means that aside from the sword, there are primordial and primitive paths for other weapons like the spear, the bow, the sabre, and many more.

And yes, two or more people can walk a primitive path, but only a single person can walk a primordial path. I don’t know how many primordial sword paths are left, but it’s safe to say that if you find another sword lady...
...Say the gate master, the universe might bless you with another path."
Kent only smiled and shook his head. It was time for him to check his next requirement in becoming a Sword Saint...
He had done enough for his master...time to cater for his needs, too...

chapters.title: Chapter 190: The Torturous Path of Genesis
paragraphs: Kent stood inside the Sword Tower with a bewildered expression. New elements had appeared, but what shocked him the most was the information displayed before him.
He had received the requirements he needed to fulfill to become a Sword Saint, and they were far from easy.
There were only three, but each one was far more challenging than he had hoped. He even questioned whether it was this difficult for everyone trying to ascend to the rank of Sword Saint.
The answer, however, was no.
While others attempting to become Sword Saints could take a decade or even several decades to complete their trials, his path alone might take far longer.
But Kent didn’t have the luxury of time.
⟪ Congratulations on becoming a Grandmaster Swords. You will now receive 2 times the speed of understanding when practicing the sword ⟫
⟪ Your Sword Qi and Sword Intent have gained a boost. You currently have 5/9 Master over Enhance Sword Qi and Sword Intent.⟫.
⟪ All forms of sword attacks using Sword Qi and Sword Intent will gain a 30% boost in attack power ⟫
Although the rewards for becoming a Grandmaster swordsman seem weak, he has, in fact, become much stronger and more dangerous. Thanks to the support from his women, every hour is a boon for him.

Additionally, his understanding of the sword has improved greatly after mastering all 10,002 sword techniques, which played a major role in his highly advanced comprehension of how to wield his sword.
But it didn’t stop there.
Beyond his understanding of the sword, he now possesses a much deeper understanding of how to execute skills and techniques perfectly.
In fact, what the Gate Master called perfect when he executed the true form of the [24 String Weaving Strike] sword skill appeared flawed to him.
Now, Kent has become someone driven by an unquenchable thirst to chase perfection on the path of the sword. He craves perfection, and as it turns out, his next requirement will push him even further.
⟪ Requirements To Become A Sword Saint... ⟫

⟪1. Master all 10,002 Sword Plays using your mind and achieve at least 7 Enlightenments. Both Sword Intent and Sword Qi must break through to the Profound Stage, and Sword Body must at least enter the Silver rank ⟫
⟪2. Cross the Sword Bridge by defeating the 13 Swordsmen using nothing but your swords, Aspects, skills and wit ⟫
⟪3. Create the foundation for three Sword Techniques, with each having the potential to become at least 7 forms of sword technique in the future ⟫
⟪ You have 6 months to complete all three requirements, else you will lose access to your Sword intent and Sword Qi for 10 years ⟫
Kent was shocked beyond comprehension. He simply couldn’t fathom how something like this could be achieved within three years.
"Gaia, tell me this won’t be measured using the time in the tower," Kent asked immediately, his tone laced with urgency. This was the most critical question.
A day on the outside equaled 24 days inside the tower, so he needed clarification.

[The Master shouldn’t worry. Just as your age is not affected by the time spent inside the tower, the duration will also remain unaffected. So, while you have six months on the outside, you will have 4,320 days, which is approximately 11.83 years inside the tower.]
"Good to know," Kent sighed.
’Eleven years... That’s how long I have to become a Sword Saint,’ Kent thought, his expression hardening with determination. He knew he had to take this seriously.
The first requirement was incredibly difficult, and the last two were not walking in the park either.
He needed to master all 10,002 sword plays using only his mind, and if that wasn’t challenging enough, he also had to achieve seven enlightenments.
"Gaia, what is this enlightenment thing? This is my first time encountering it," Kent asked. He could sense it was something profound and important, so he asked early to prepare accordingly.
[Enlightenment is the most important part of every swordsman’s journey. In fact, any swordsman who has not encountered or gone through enlightenment before cannot be deemed a true swordsman.

In the sword path, sword enlightenment begins when one becomes a Sword Grandmaster. At the Grandmaster stage, one’s understanding of the sword starts to grow. In the path of the sword, they might reach a level of understanding that forces them to enter the stage of enlightenment.

At this stage, they must undergo at least three instances of enlightenment before breaking through to the Sword Saint stage. Gaining enlightenment is entering a state where your understand will undergo a qualitative change]
"Wait a minute. Only three? Then why am I required to do seven?" Kent asked, frustration creeping into his voice.
He didn’t know why he felt that way, but deep down, he could tell that attaining enlightenment wouldn’t be easy. So why seven for him and only three for everyone else?
[The keyword there is at least. Seven is for master. This means, in some cases, the number can vary, especially since there are thirteen Sword Enlightenment stages, each with its own unique nature.]
"...Unbelievable," Kent sighed, shaking his head.
Aside from the enlightenment, Kent also had to upgrade his sword qi and sword intent to the Profound stage, as well as advance his sword body to the Silver stage.
He was currently at the Copper stage/rank. Thankfully, he now had body cultivation to rely on. But still, the requirements were just too strict.
’At this stage, I wonder what kind of requirements I’ll face when becoming a Sword Sage...’ Kent smiled to himself and made a mental note to use his charm to fill his large bed with beauties.
Having beauties to spend time with when he was tired from training would, without a doubt, make things much simpler and easier.
"Then how about the sword bridge?" Kent asked.

[For that, you have to cross it. Like in the description, you must defeat the 13 swordsmen. But you must know this: the 13 swordsmen are measured based on how much progress you should have made at a given point in time.
So, let’s say you have mastered 1,000 swordplays and moved your sword qi and intent to 7/9; the swordsman you will be facing will be measured using this metric.
However, it will also be measured based on the tower’s expectations and some other unknown variables.]
"So in other words, the tower is going to fuck me up," Kent laughed, staring daggers at Gaia, who was looking at him with an expression that said, "I have no idea this is going to fuck up."
Kent just sighed.
He moved and appeared before the Sword Bridge, which stretched many miles across the landscape.
It was a large sword filled with Sword Will, the same will coming from the Sword of Enlightenment, infused with the 10,002 swordplays.
"So all I have to do is keep mastering the swordplays and then I can walk across this bridge, right?" Kent asked, and Gaia nodded.
Something told him he shouldn’t dare step on it if he didn’t want to experience true pain. He could only relax and wait for the moment when he could contend with it.
"I guess I will start challenging core disciples now... This will make things much easier for me when I face this bridge," Kent made his plan.
If only he knew that when Gaia mentioned there would be some unknown variables, one of the variables was the fact that the 13 swordsmen would all have Sword Saint-level understanding and mastery...
He is screwed...

chapters.title: Chapter 191: Body Tower, Golden Titan Stairway
paragraphs: [As for the third requirement, you will have to build the foundation for three sword techniques that will become integral to the future requirements and your future as a swordsman.

Just three, but very essential. My advice, however, is for you first to master all 10,002 sword plays, push your aspects to the requirements, and have at least six enlightenments. Then, if possible, defeat at least seven swordsmen in the sword bridge before attempting this.

You will have many more days and chances to visualize your desired sword technique. Also, it will be best to venture into mind cultivation early, as your mental capacity will be required to form these three foundations.
In fact, it’s a crucial aspect that you will need to start visualizing a sword technique that has the potential to house seven different forms.]
Kent nodded.
The current him would mess this up if he chose to dive into it now. He must first grow...and the only way for him to grow is to do more fighting and a deeper understanding of the path of the sword...
[That said, the master must really fight more since that is the best way to grow as a swordsman. You must face odds far greater than yours if you want to walk the Genesis path... trust me.]
Kent nodded again. He chose to move away after walking around the Sword of Enlightenment. His next destination was the Body Tower, which he had awakened when he became a body cultivator.
He couldn’t enter to tell what he had received or even review the message since, back then, he was just trying to break through to the Sword Grandmaster stage.
"Wow."
Kent was taken aback when he appeared inside the Body Tower. It was not at all like he had envisioned.
Inside was a grassy field with nothing but a large, tall golden staircase housing no less than ten thousand steps.
[This is the Golden Titan Stairway. Although you temper your body to make it much more steady and durable, you must also temper it under pressure.
On the Golden Titan Stairway, you will experience pressure as you climb. The higher you climb, the greater the pressure increases.
There are 10,002 steps, and each has its own percentage of increase in pressure. But the moment you move past a step, you won’t feel any pressure later when you pass it.]
"I see. This makes more sense now. With this, my chances of becoming a Bronze body will be achieved much faster."
"Indeed. These stairs are ideal for the master and his women. With these stairs, they will benefit more as they temper their bodies."
Kent nodded.
’But something ain’t adding up’
Kent started to ponder on something. The stairs were good, but he felt like something was off. So he asked Gaia. As the master of the towers, he knew when someone was being deceived.
"Gaia, I doubt this stairway is meant for just climbing under pressure. There must be more to it...right?"

Gaia looked at Kent and smiled. She seemed to have expected the question, but she wasn’t aware Kent would ask it this early. She took out that information from the messages she showed him when she awakened the Body Tower.
She had wanted it to be a surprise, but it seemed Kent was much more perceptive.

[Indeed. There is more to the stairway. The 10,002 steps are divided into 7 stages. The first stage has 300 steps. If you manage to finish a stage, you will receive a Mystical-grade tempering treasure that you can use to further temper your body.
But aside from that, for every 100 steps you climb, you will receive random body-tempering treasures ranging from Earth grade to Legendary grade.]

Kent smiled upon hearing that. Of course, he could go ahead and ask for some of these items, but he just doesn’t want to. Like how Gaia wanted to surprise him with these boons, he also wanted to surprise himself.
Kent walked close to the stairway and casually stepped on the first step. As soon as his leg touched it, he felt a change in the gravity pressing down on him.
He added the other leg but managed to remain standing.
He then moved to the second step, and like the first, the pressure changed, but he was able to withstand it. He quickly moved through the steps until he arrived at the 10th step.
That’s where he felt the pressure increase much more. He could feel he was being pressed down by a force so great that he just didn’t have the strength to move his leg.
[The master must know nothing is easy in the tower. To become a monster, you must undergo monstrous training], Gaia said with a smug expression.
Kent just sat down and started to cultivate under the pressure. He knew that to move forward, he must first become accustomed to the pressure.
After 20 minutes, his body adapted to the pressure, so he moved to the 11th step. Strangely, the pressure wasn’t as intense, so he moved ahead, and within an hour, he was on the 15th step.
He used another hour to get to the 19th step. By the 19th step, Kent finally understood why they said body cultivation is expensive.

Right now, he knew he needed loads of herbs and resources to keep tempering his body. He recognized how weak he was and how much he must improve if he wanted to always have an edge in battle... even against those stronger than him.
[The master can always visit the store to get top-notch resources. I might even give you a discount.]
Gaia joked, hovering before Kent, who was adapting to the pressure on the 19th step. He didn’t mind her and just focused for 2 hours before he adapted.
Then he moved to the 20th, but when he stepped on it, he felt a great pressure fall down on him, forcing him to move his leg back to the 19th step.
"Damn... My bones nearly broke."

[Oh, I forgot to tell Master. Every 10 steps increase the pressure by 2. This means if the pressure on the 19th step can restrict your body, then the pressure on the 20th step can break your bones, the 30th can shatter your bones, and the 40th will grind them to powder.]
Kent sighed and then stepped on the 20th step again. He gritted his teeth and endured the pressure until he managed to step on the 20th step with both legs.
He was immediately sent down onto his knees, forcing him to kneel. He took the pressure and went into a lotus posture, beginning to cultivate the pressure.
Before he realized it, a day had passed, yet the pressure was still there... Though he had adapted somewhat, it was by a small percentage. So, he continued to cultivate...
Three days later, he finally managed to stand and move around on the 20th step. The step was large enough to fit more than 100 people at the same time.
He moved around slowly at first, but after a while, he was running, which made him very confident. But like they say, you should tap out when it’s still favorable for you.

Kent didn’t move to the 21st step. Instead, he chose to leave the tower for now. He still had to visit the Spear Saintess, but first, he needed to know more about the sect, and who better to take him around than Ingrid, his next target?
Though they didn’t know each other, Kent planned to take it slowly by getting to know her first. He would just let her play with little Kent if worst came to shove.
If only he knew, despite Ingrid’s desire to have his divine rod inside her, she would want Kent to gain her master’s permission first.

Kent dressed up and went out to meet Ingrid, who had been expecting him for hours now.
"Are you alright? Are the injuries gone?" she asked the moment Kent appeared. Her master had wrecked him a while ago, so she was checking to see if he was still breathing.
"I am fine. But I will have to pay her back for torturing me," Kent said.
"Good luck with that. Master is no easy fish you can fry," she said with a proud smile. Kent just smiled and sat down facing her.
"So...Do you want to be my guide and show me around the sect. I am new and I doubt after the events that happened a few days ago, any elder or disciple will be willing to do that," Kent asked.
"I don’t mind. But know that walking around with me comes with some dangers," Ingrid said, making Kent smile.
"I don’t mind trouble. But are you sure you want to be seen with me? I mean, everyone probably wants me dead by now," Kent asked, but Ingrid just shrugged.
"I’ll be fine," she replied.
"Then let’s go. I want to come back early and help my master with something," Kent said with a smile.

Ingrid, who may have understood the reference, blushed slightly. Her mind immediately drifted back to when she first encountered Kent... and an image of his body flashed unbidden into her thoughts, making her blush deepen.
Kent smirked and started moving away from the mini-mansion.
"You are very bold, Kent... I never expected the Sword Saintess to ever fall in love with anything or anyone aside from her sword," Ingrid said as they began moving away.
"What can I say? She saw a magnificent dragon she shouldn’t have." Kent gave her a smug smile. Ingrid just shook her head to wipe the images from her mind.
"So, what is your background, Kent?" Ingrid suddenly asked after recovering.
"Wow, aren’t we moving a little too fast?" Kent stopped and looked at her.
"What do you mean we’re moving too fast? I just wanted to know more about your background," Ingrid looked at him strangely.

"I mean, shouldn’t you tell me something about yourself first? Where I come from, before you try to ask for someone’s identity, you must at least share something about yourself first," Kent said, shaking his head.
"That just doesn’t make sense. I merely asked for your identity. That doesn’t mean anything," Ingrid said, sounding confused.

Kent smiled and became technical. "Maybe in your own way, you don’t see it like that. But look at it this way: when you’re trying to get to know someone, they might feel more comfortable opening up to you if they know something about you first.
I mean, if I outright ask you about your background, will you reveal it?" Kent asked.
"Yes," Ingrid replied, making Kent take a step back thoughtfully.
"That is unexpected but, in a way, also very disturbing," Kent laughed, but Ingrid grew serious, not understanding what he found amusing.
[Master, I think you might have just found yourself someone they call a nerd in your previous world,] Gaia said, echoing what Kent had just realized.

Ingrid was indeed a genius... perhaps a little too good for her own good. She took everything literally, which, in a way, was both a strength and a weakness. Having such a direct mindset wasn’t exactly ideal...
Imagine taking everything literally, including how you present yourself.
"Ah, forget it," Kent succumbed. Ingrid was a beauty, and having such a side only made her cuter.
’Maybe I should get her a pair of glasses to complete her makeover as a nerd,’ Kent thought. Meanwhile, Gaia, who overheard, was already searching the cosmos for the perfect glasses.

"Well, I am Kent Madson... single child, no relatives because I have none. My parents are dead and left me with tons of wealth—enough to buy a kingdom or two. I like being around beautiful ladies such as yourself, and I don’t shy away from making my feelings known.
"I am also a grandmaster swordsman, and while you shouldn’t tell anyone, I am also an alchemist."

Kent smiled as he said that. Well, his relatives were currently basking in the tons of wealth he had left back on Earth. In his will, he gave everything to his aunt, who had been close to his mother while she was alive.
"That is impressive, but until I see you concoct a pill, I wouldn’t believe you’re an alchemist. And I’m sorry for your loss," Ingrid smiled warmly.

"Thanks for your concern, but I’m over it. That said, truly, don’t tell anyone I’m an alchemist. If you do, I wouldn’t hesitate to lock you up for a couple of years in my special prison," Kent said in a joking tone, though he was serious.

"Then do you want to know about me?" Ingrid asked. Kent just smiled; he had already captured her information a couple of days ago and knew almost everything there was to know about her, down to her likes and dislikes.
"Sure... I would love to know more about you," But he wasn’t about to deny her the chance to share more about herself...
Ingrid, of course, began telling him more about her lineage. However, Kent, who started listening, began doubting some of the details his enchanted eyes revealed.
[This nerdy cat is very complex, Master. If I were you, I wouldn’t let her slip through my fingers.] The perverted Gaia said what Kent was also thinking as he learned more about Ingrid.

You may have received a crystal token from your master. That token is where your points are stored and can be used to buy food, skill books, and other necessary resources while inside and from the sect.

"Of course, if you’re rich , you can go outside and buy them using spirit stones, but while inside the sect, you must and will only be able to spend Divine points," Ingrid said, making Kent take out the crystal token he received from his master.
"Strange, why do I have 10,000 points? Is that normal?" Kent asked, and Ingrid stopped to look at his crystal. Indeed, he had 10,000 points. This made her shake her head.
"Looks like your master didn’t want you to suffer, so she gave you this much. My master only gave me 500 when I became her disciple," Ingrid sighed, making Kent realize that perhaps he was fortunate.
"I will thank her properly when I get back," Kent licked his lips, making Ingrid scoff before she started moving.
They were still on their way from his master’s mansion toward the inner area of the Sword Gate.
"Say, I want more points. How do I get them?" Kent asked.
"You earn points from missions. In the sect, there are various missions you can pick from that will earn you some points. Most of these missions are internal, but some are external.
In your case, most of your missions will be external since you are an Inner Disciple and a Grandmaster Swordsman. That said, missions are also structured as Low, Medium, and High in the inner area.

There are very High, Calamity and Hell missions in the Core Area. Though you will find out soon enough, it’s best if you pick a medium mission for now. High missions are too dangerous and wouldn’t be ideal for someone at your current status."
"What is that supposed to mean?" Kent gave her the ’bruh’ look, making Ingrid smile.
"Missions from the High grade upward are just too dangerous for someone of your status. I’m not looking down on you. I’m just telling you the facts.

Take, for example, a mission to accompany a merchant family from one kingdom to the next through the Dark Forest. You won’t only be on the lookout for bandits; you’ll also have to handle beast attacks.
While in some cases, you can be lucky and sail through smoothly, those are just rare occasions.
So, you might want to take on a Medium mission for now and handle the tougher ones later. Of course, if you want, you can pick the mission as a team, but in the end, you’ll have to share the points."
"I see. That is informative, and I will do well to know my level," Kent nodded. "But in case you need a teammate, don’t hesitate to let me know."
Ingrid nodded. She was already considering it, given that she had never met someone with Kent’s talent. Of course, she also wasn’t about to pull him into a Very High mission... Not just yet.
"Then aside from missions, is there a way for me to earn Divine Points?" Kent asked. Surely, there must be a way.

"Yes, there is indeed a way. There are two more ways, actually. The first one is to go to the duel hall and pick a duel challenge. Most inner and core disciples like to show off their skills and talents, so they place challenges.
This challenge comes with a price tag. If you win, you earn those prizes.
As for the second one, it’s more like the sect will sponsor you to bring them glory by accepting challenges from other sects that want to show off their disciples.
Mostly, these challenges are arranged by the various Gate Masters for their disciples, but if you want, you can pick one up from the duel hall, and the sect will make it happen."
"...Hmm, looks like this place won’t be boring at all. I guess I will pick a few challenges when I am done learning more about this place."
Kent was genuinely happy so far with what Ingrid had revealed to him. He wanted a challenge to practice more, so having these many options would surely be useful.
"If you want a challenge, you can enter the upcoming Sect competition in 4 months’ time.
Only core disciples will be participating, considering this is just the preliminary event to select the 12 who will represent the kingdom in the Kingdom Genius Competition.

"But if you want to be part of the team being formed by the sect, then you can apply. I don’t know the current requirements, but you will be subjected to a test, and if you pass, you can secure a spot.
However, you must understand that the sect already has its team, so to earn a slot, you must prove that you are highly capable."
Kent nodded.

Soon, they were in the Inner area of the Sword Gate, where word began spreading the moment they saw Kent. In fact, everyone seemed to have been waiting for days just to report on his appearance after the duel.
While they were busy reporting, Ingrid led Kent out of the Sword Gate and toward the Spear Gate since Kent was there both for a tour and to meet Spear Saintess Neomi, who was expecting him.
"It seems you are much more famous than I thought," Ingrid said as they moved from the Sword Gate into the Spear Gate.
Kent could only smile, watching as hundreds of people began reporting on his sudden appearance. He, of course, didn’t mind and simply continued moving through with Ingrid.
The moment they entered the Spear Gate, Kent sensed a powerful aura locking onto him. He immediately recognized who it belonged to but just shrugged.
It seemed the Sword Gate Master was somehow taking asylum in the Spear Gate after Kent and his Master had refused to see her a couple of times already.
’This lady just doesn’t give up, does she?’ Kent said inwardly.
[Maybe the master should just tame her,] Gaia said, making Kent trip. Luckily, Ingrid caught him before he could fall.
Unfortunately, this sudden closeness was captured by some disciples, who immediately began spreading the word that Kent and Ingrid were dating.
This made many very angry, one of them being Randy, the guy who was with Ingrid when she first met Kent at the Silver Leaf auction house.

chapters.title: Chapter 194: Tasty Home Pavilion
paragraphs: "Big Brother Randy... Big Brother Randy!" In a certain lush apartment somewhere in the Core area of the Spear Gate, an inner disciple ran toward Randy’s apartment, which may have ultimately disrupted his cultivation.
Randy’s face contorted into anger, but he lightened up a bit when he saw the young man. This young man was one of the few who had chosen to become his retainers in the sect.
"What is it, Maxwell... why the sudden frantic visit?" Randy asked, putting away his spear. He and Ingrid were some of the top core disciples in the Spear Gate and, ultimately, the sect.
"We have a big problem, Big Brother Randy," Maxwell said, making Randy fully focus his attention on him.
"Spill it..."

"You remember the kid who won the Trial of the Sword a couple of days ago? He was just spotted with Big Sister Ingrid, and from the way they were moving and handling each other, everyone started calling them a couple."
Maxwell wasn’t even done when Randy’s face contorted back to that of extreme anger. He didn’t like what he had just heard.

Well, nobody would like to hear that their crush—someone they had dedicated most of their life to—was seen with another man, and now many had placed a label on them. In fact, he hadn’t earned that label yet despite spending years chasing after her.
"Do you know where this brat is?" Randy asked.
"They were heading toward Tasty Home Pavilion... I’m sure they’re going to have dinner," Maxwell said, wasting no effort to add more fuel to the fire.
As expected, Randy started moving away, definitely going to Tasty Home Pavilion. Maxwell ran after him while calling a few minions to meet them there.

Meanwhile, Kent and Ingrid, who had moved through the Spear Gate while he was keeping his attention on the Sword Gate Master, had finally arrived in front of a large restaurant that also acted as a hotel or an inn of some kind.
"This is the Tasty Home Pavilion... If you’re looking to get the best food rich in essence to eat, this is where you get it," Ingrid said, and Kent nodded.

"But why is it in the Spear Gate? Does it mean only disciples from the Spear Gate can eat here?" Kent asked. "And why would they have hotel services if they’re in a sect where disciples already have homes?"
Ingrid looked at him with a ’bruh’ expression.
"This is not an establishment of the sect. It’s an outside business, and while it shouldn’t be here, it’s the sect’s way of giving the disciples a chance to still experience the outside life here.
Spirit stones are spent here, and as for the rooms, there are many uses for them. Just because you’re living in the best place in the sect doesn’t mean everyone is."
"Also, the reason why it’s in the Spear Gate—or, more importantly, appears to be in the Spear Gate—is that the Spear Gate is the center of the sect. It was only natural to put it here."
"I see... That makes some sense," Kent nodded. He knew what she said was indeed true. He got to live with his master in a lavish house, but not everyone has that.
So, while some might not have Divine Points, using spirit stones here is the way.
The rich and privileged will get to show off their wealth here. Kent knew it was the best thing that the sect could come up with.
Of course, this also means the divine points that are critical can now be spent on something much more beneficial.
"Of course, if a plate of rice costs a spirit stone on the outside, here, it costs a hundred... So still, not many would want to come here," Ingrid added, and Kent just smiled.
"Let’s grab a bite... I’m kinda hungry and need some energy," Kent suggested. Ingrid didn’t immediately reply, causing Kent to ask why.

"You do know we’re being followed, and I’m sure some core disciples are part of those following us. The moment we step inside this restaurant, the sect rules will lose their effect inside... This means we can be attacked, or in your case, you can be attacked," Ingrid explained. Kent just shrugged.
"Who cares about those idiots... I just want to eat, so they can come... I doubt they’ll be able to do much," Kent said before taking Ingrid’s hand and leading her inside.
A couple of meters away, the disciples who saw this seethed in anger and also started creeping closer to the restaurant.

Of course, not all of them would be able to enter, considering that the entrance fee could buy them loads of cultivation resources on the outside. In fact, 80% of the disciples following wouldn’t be able to do anything to him since they couldn’t enter.
Kent didn’t know this, but he was thrilled to see there was a place where he could spend his money while inside the sect.
They moved through the yard of the restaurant and soon arrived at the entrance.
"You must pay an entrance fee of 80,000, or if you have 100,000 spirit stones, you can buy a membership," Ingrid said to him before taking out a silver badge.
"What grade is that?" Kent asked, though he already knew the answer.
In fact, he had used his enchanted eyes on the restaurant, which was how he discovered there are membership levels in Tasty Home Pavilion.
They have Silver, Gold, Diamond, and Platinum memberships. Of course, the prices are also exaggerated, but having a membership is beneficial.
You can use it in any Tasty Home Pavilion on the human continent. It’s like the badge Alina gave to Kent. It will allow him to enter any Silver Leaf Auction house On the human continent.
"Mine is the lowest grade, and I only got that thanks to being the disciple of a Saintess," Ingrid said before showing it to the staff at the entrance.𝗳𝚛𝗲𝕖𝚠𝚎𝚋𝗻𝗼𝕧𝗲𝐥.𝚌𝚘𝐦
"I’ll see you inside," Ingrid smiled and stepped in. She could have brought him inside, but she wanted to see if what Saintess Selene said was true.
She wanted to know if Kent was indeed rich. Though she wasn’t a gold digger, she was also very curious about his background.
"Please, I’d like to buy a membership," Kent said to the staff. The staff scanned Kent’s appearance, but the bastard was too handsome for them to assume his status, so they nodded and led him away.
Ingrid, who saw this, simply waited for him to return.
Kent was led to a room where he was greeted by a certain lady with a rather impressive chest. In fact, had she been wearing a buttoned shirt, those poor buttons would have been suffering by now.
Kent sat down, and they began their discussion.
Meanwhile, a couple of kilometers outside the restaurant, angry disciples are already gathered and ready to see if the bastards who took their beauty can be hacked into pieces.
One had to say that these disciples certainly have a lot of time on their hands. I mean, why would anyone even bother to come, knowing not even Ingrid’s shadow would take them as her boyfriend?
They are just wasting their time for nothing, and it is vivid now, showing how incompetent people can be.
If Ingrid can only marry one man, then why would they waste their time, knowing all too well she wouldn’t give them a second glance?
But then again, this is just how people are... Some are there to suck up to the core disciples who have a shot at making Ingrid their woman.
Well... that was their assumption.

chapters.title: Chapter 195: Platinum Customer
paragraphs: "So those are the memberships we offer. The Tasty Home Pavilion is a continent-wide establishment, so no matter where you go on the human continent, you can use it. In fact, having a membership will even give you some benefits in other establishments," said the heavy-chested manager of the restaurant.
Though she knew nothing about Kent, the fact that he walked in with a member holding even just a silver badge was enough to tell her he was not simple.
"Then, can I know the prices for each membership?" Kent asked.
"The silver membership is 100,000 spirit stones. This will allow you access to the first three floors. Additionally, it permits one person to accompany you.
The gold membership is 1,000,000 spirit stones. This grants you access to the first five floors. You can also bring two people with you, each of whom will receive gold membership treatment.
The diamond membership is 10,000,000 spirit stones. With this, you will have access to the first eight floors and can bring five people with you.
Furthermore, this card allows you to stay for as long as you want in our hotels and inns across the continent for free.
You will also gain access to other services we provide and even have the opportunity to request a personal cook.
As for the platinum membership, which is our highest tier, it costs 100 million spirit stones. With this, you can access the top floor of the ninth floor.
You will receive a 70% discount on all food and free services such as hotels, massages, and even security, which can include multiple Root Transcendents at no cost.
There are numerous freebies you will receive at any establishment we own. In fact, with the platinum membership, you can bring up to 30 people with you, and none of them will be required to pay fees.
Additionally, with the platinum membership, any customer you recommend will receive a 30% discount on all memberships."
Kent listened to all the amazing packages, and a smile appeared on his face. The manager saw the smile and smiled back.
She held an expectant gaze, which showed she was really hoping Kent would buy a membership, earning her a huge commission.
If only she knew Kent was about to change her life.
"I will be buying a Platinum Membership. Also, kindly upgrade the membership of the lady I came with to the Platinum grade," Kent said casually.
The manager froze in her seat.
Kent said something, and her mind couldn’t process it immediately.
"Did-did you just say you want a platinum membership?" she asked in a bated breath.
Kent looked at her expression and smiled.
"Yeah. You know what they say, you must impress the beauties by showing off your wealth," Kent smirked, saying that. There was no saying like that... he just didn’t know what to do with his money.

He could buy most of the things he needed with Tower Points, so spirit stones were like something he could use on the side. It was like how cultivators view gold coins these days...it is worthless to him...at least for now.
Well, doing things like this was what he could use spirit stones for. So, as they say, the more you have, the less you know how to spend it.
The manager kept staring at Kent—not because she was admiring his handsomeness, but because she was shocked beyond her wits and couldn’t process how to proceed.
"Take your time," Kent said, leaning back in his chair as he waited for the manager to recover. Naturally, it took her a full minute.
"Right away," she said, pulling a jade token from her space ring and injecting spiritual qi into it. Then she began asking Kent for his details. Whenever Kent answered, the token would glow.

A couple of seconds later, the process was done, and she entered an inner office. When she walked out, she was holding yet another jade token. However, this one was much more elegant and golden in color.
"Here you go, and this is for your lady friend," she said, handing the tokens to Kent, who accepted them and continued to stare at her.
He was looking to see if she would understand why he was staring, but she seemed clueless. Kent smiled and said,
"Next time, compose yourself well before handing over such expensive jade crystals to a stranger without taking the money first."
Kent took two pouches from his space ring and handed them to her. She received them with trembling hands. Kent simply smiled like an overly privileged rich kid and left the office.
The manager put the money away and ran after him, her movements causing her ample chest to bounce up and down. Kent was walking ahead of her, so he couldn’t see such an elegant sight.

"Distinguished customer, because you are our first Platinum customer, you will enjoy free food for the next 30 days. No matter how much you eat or how much you bring with you, it will be free," the manager said, her tone shifting.
She had indeed earned a significant profit thanks to Kent, so she ensured his stay at the Tasty Home Pavilion would be smooth.
"Then I will take you up on the freebie," Kent replied, still walking. A hundred million spirit stones were not something to be underestimated—not in the slightest.

So, for him to have poured out close to 200 million spirit stones was simply too overwhelming, to say the least. Kent had to be the richest person she had encountered since becoming the manager or even since she started working at the Tasty Home Pavilion.
’I need to inform the pavilion mistress of this... This young man is not simple... She would want to know more about him and perhaps extend an invitation to him,’ she thought.
"You’re back," Ingrid said, looking strangely at Kent, who was smiling at her.
"Yeah... Sorry for making you wait so long," Kent said before turning to the manager. "Can you lead us to the ninth floor? I’m very hungry and would love to have a bite."
The manager nodded...
Ingrid, however, was shocked when she heard Kent’s request. "The ninth floor is for platinum members..." She paused and looked at him. "Don’t tell me you have a Platinum membership."
Kent smiled. "What can I say? The heavens wouldn’t forgive me if I don’t give a fairy such as yourself the best treatment." He retrieved the golden jade crystal token.
"You’re also a platinum member now, so good luck enjoying all the benefits." He handed the badge to her, causing Ingrid’s body to stiffen upon contact with it.
The manager watched all this with a complicated expression. It was a simple exchange, but she could swear she sensed no intimate air between them.
’So, did he just buy the membership because they are friends?’ she wondered.
Haha... If only she knew the Chaos Dragon was playing games, she would have looked at him in a completely new light.

Ingrid struggled with the idea that she was now a platinum member. However, she didn’t get to stay in her trance for long, as Kent dragged her away to the ninth floor, where they entered a private room and began to enjoy themselves.
Kent was rather hungry despite being a cultivator who could go months without food. Well, he is from Earth, after all...
On the outside, however, the angry disciples appeared... but all they would encounter was great disappointment.

chapters.title: Chapter 196: Money Stops Nonsense
paragraphs: Right after the manager sent Kent and Ingrid to the ninth floor, she immediately descended and gathered the workers.
"We just registered our first-ever Platinum customers," she said, bringing shocked expressions to everyone’s faces.
As she mentioned, they had registered their first-ever platinum customer, which was shocking considering that for years now, the highest they have registered was just a Gold membership.
This was huge for them, as under no circumstances would someone typically pay a hundred million spirit stones just to become a member of their establishment.

Of course, they had platinum members, but not in a sect—not just any sect. So, this was kind of a big deal for them. Now, inside the Tasty Home Pavilion, Kent and Ingrid held higher authority than even the sect leader, primarily because of their membership levels.
"I’m telling you this mainly because of the crowd outside. I hope you all know what to do," the manager said before leaving.
"Unbelievable, to think we will ever have our first Platinum customers," a worker said, looking shocked.
"Who is this new Platinum customer, though?" another worker asked.
"I saw a certain handsome fella and Lady Ingrid enter the pavilion a couple of minutes ago, and later, Lady Erika led them away. I’m sure it’s them."
"To think Lady Ingrid’s boyfriend will be this rich," a certain lady worker said with a hint of envy in her tone.
"Cut it, Jane. You and I are just workers... Fantasies like this will never happen to us," another worker said, making the worker named Jane roll her eyes.
"I know. I just didn’t expect something like this to happen. She mostly comes here with Disciple Randy... I wonder how he will react when he hears of this new development."
Obviously, this lady is the type of worker who likes to spread rumors. She would, without a doubt, stay close to the chaos to handle the gossip mill later.
The workers dispersed to their work, with some serving the two Platinum customers on the ninth floor. Of course, they never expected their Platinum customers to have such a rich appetite.
...Well, it was Kent who was eating. Ingrid was still so shocked that all she could do was stare at Kent as he cleared one bowl after another.
He wasn’t concerned about the fact that he had spent enough money that could be used to buy a couple of Heaven-grade skills and weapons.
"You... who are you?" Ingrid finally asked, but Kent was busy chewing, so she had to wait.
"You already know my name, but since you asked, I’ll introduce myself again," Kent said, gulping down a juice made from some of the rarest fruits rich in spiritual qi.
"The name is Kent. Kent Madson... 18 years old, and I happen to be the richest person in the whole world," Kent said shamelessly.
Of course, Ingrid knew he was just messing with her, but she couldn’t help but think that perhaps there was some truth in what he said.
And it’s true, though.

Kent is perhaps the richest in the entire world. He has things inside his tower that he can easily use to multiply his wealth manifold, so the concept of whether or not he is rich—even he doesn’t know how rich he can become if he chases after wealth.
"You have to eat... My auntie said if you don’t eat, you’ll grow lean," Kent said before going back to digging in.
Ingrid continued to stare at him for a couple of minutes before she chose to eat something so she wouldn’t grow lean from being shocked and witless.
She is from a merchant family that could be ranked among the richest, considering they are into auction houses, buying and selling.
But she couldn’t spend 170 million spirit stones like that...

"What do you mean that brat isn’t here?" a disciple asked, holding a silver badge showing he is a Silver member. The Gold members have a light gold badge made from ordinary crystal, while the Platinum badge is made from a rare jade crystal.
This disciple is just a lackey sent to discover where Kent is. Randy sent him, and as such, with his shoulders high, he came ready to investigate and report back.
"Like I said, the one you are looking for is not here," the worker at the entrance said, not even bothering to look at the badge in his hand.
"We clearly saw him enter the pavilion a couple of minutes ago... so what the hell do you mean he’s not here? Are you looking to lose your job?" the disciple said, raising his voice.
This immediately attracted the attention of the other workers.
"What seems to be the problem?" the gossiping-type worker asked.
The disciple, who was acting all high and mighty, looked at her with disdain evident on his face. To him, holding a Silver badge was the highest authority one could brag about.

In the sect, only Randy and a few core disciples have the Gold badge, which allows them to climb to the 5th floor. Of course, they bought those mainly to impress the ladies, with Ingrid being their main target.

"A brat entered this establishment a couple of minutes ago. I doubt he has what it takes to even pay the entrance fee. Now, if you don’t want to get into trouble, I demand you tell me where he is," the disciple said arrogantly.
The workers who heard his words clenched their fists, with a few ready to jump him and beat the crap out of him. However, the elegant and poised Randy entered before they could do that.
"Maxwell, you shouldn’t behave like that. These fine people are just doing their job," Randy said, walking inside.
Following him were a few other core and inner disciples, both male and female. Of course, the males were after Kent while the ladies were there to throw jabs at Ingrid.
"But Big Brother Randy, I just wanted to know where that brat is so I could tell him my mind," Maxwell said, looking offended.
Of course, even an idiot would know the two were in cahoots.

"It’s okay," Randy said before taking out his gold badge. "I demand to know where the fellow who entered with Disciple Ingrid is. He stole something from me, and I want it back," Randy declared, showing his badge.
The workers exchanged looks, none willing to shatter his hopes and dreams just yet. Of course, the entrance worker wasn’t one to have much patience, so he took the lead.
"I am sorry, but you don’t have the qualification to know where he is."
"What do you mean I don’t have the qualification? I am a gold member," Randy asked arrogantly.
"Yes...you are a gold customer. If you want to know where he is, you’ll need to upgrade your membership to Platinum. Only then will you have the qualification to ask about a platinum customer."
"WHAT?" All the disciples who entered held their jaws in disbelief when they heard Kent was a platinum customer. That was a shocker.
Randy, who had been arrogant, now wore a shocked expression on his face. He simply couldn’t believe his ears. Kent, his love rival, is a platinum customer...
’How is he going to compete with that?’
Of course, Kent, who had been waiting for that moment, suddenly spoke a few words from the ninth floor.

"You know what they say, money stops nonsense," his voice dripped with ridicule. He had been aiming for this very moment—to anger a few core disciples, provoke them into challenging him, and then beat them up.
"Since I’m feeling generous today, I’ll be donating 500 million to the Pavilion. All I ask is that you send out the noise-makers so I can enjoy my meal in peace."

chapters.title: Chapter 197: Sudden Challenge
paragraphs: A wise man once said, "The coming is easy, simple, and vigorous... However, it’s the going after a blatant disrespect that is hard."
Right now, that is exactly how Randy and his minions are feeling. They came with their shoulders held high, ready to destroy a brat who seemed to be after their jewel.

But instead of having their way, their pride and dreams are now shattered beyond repair. Not only are they unable to do anything to him, but they also risk losing their memberships—something they cannot afford.
Kent laughed, his voice dripping with ridicule...

"Let me guess... You losers came here thinking you could use your wealth to have your way. Lol... Sometimes I forget how poor these rich and overly privileged kids can be," Kent said, glancing at Ingrid, who was looking back at him with a shocked expression.
"Sorry, fellas, I am richer than your families combined, so next time, cut your coat according to your size," Kent said. He wasn’t ready to let this slide.

He knew from high school that if you let your bullies keep bullying you for long, they would see themselves as supreme. So he made it clear now—he wasn’t about to let the rich and privileged have their way with him.
They had money, but he was richer. He could only watch them despair since they couldn’t beat him in that field.
As expected, the manager came and gently led the disciples out. She wasn’t about to pass up on 500 million.
If there are rich brats, then there is a rich, arrogant chaos dragon currently willing to give her 500 million. She will become the employee of the decade at this point.
After Randy and his minions were led away, Ingrid sighed.
"You do know that after leaving this place, everyone will want to kill you, right?" she said, but Kent just brushed it off.

"They shouldn’t opt for a deathmatch, though. Defeating them will suffice, considering I don’t want to anger some truly dangerous people, like the Tower Masters, by going on a killing spree," Kent said, taking his last bite.
"Are you looking down on core disciples?" Ingrid asked.
"No... but I don’t think they should look down on me, though. You know what they say, appearances can be deceiving sometimes."
Of course, Kent was looking down on them. It was his arrogance getting the best of him.
But if you were to ask whether he had the qualifications to look down on them... the answer is yes. Most of the core disciples have just entered the next stage of their cultivation.
Most were at the peak of the Root Sage cultivation realm, with a few already at the Root Great Sage realm. However, none could boast of possessing prowess like Kent.
In the path of swordsmanship, he possessed all three Aspects: Sword Qi, Sword Intent, and Sword Body. That alone was enough for him to compare himself to a Sword Saint.
"You should be careful... I can’t save you from everyone," Ingrid said, bringing a smile to Kent’s face.
"The fact that you even consider saving me makes all the difference here," Kent said, teasing her. As expected, Ingrid blushed slightly, but she turned away from him.
"I only hope you can be this arrogant later on." Ingrid stood up and was ready to leave, but Kent held her hand and dragged her closer to him before holding onto her waist.
He moved her closer to himself and gently brushed his thumb across her lips before licking it... The action was so seductive that Ingrid’s body shuddered in his grip.𝒇𝒓𝙚𝒆𝔀𝓮𝓫𝒏𝓸𝙫𝓮𝓵.𝓬𝙤𝙢
"You should pay attention to how you eat... You wouldn’t want to leave food remains on your lips," Kent said, still holding her close to his body.
Ingrid, who had been in a state of shock throughout the dinner, wasn’t aware of the food that remained stuck to her lips.
Kent smiled at her expression and then let go of her waist, making sure his hands brushed across her butt, giving it a gentle massage.
Ingrid’s body shuddered again, but Kent just smiled and dragged her away, holding her hand. Now that he was done eating, he could only continue with the tour.
"Here you go, as promised," Kent said, handing over the 500 million spirit stones to the manager under the shocked expressions of all the workers present.
"I really enjoyed the food here. I will come back soon, perhaps with a few friends. I hope we will be treated well." The manager and the workers nodded.
Kent nodded back at them and walked away, holding Ingrid’s hand. The workers could only stare at him with gazes filled with reverence.
500 million... each worker would be earning a couple of millions then. They were super excited.
The manager quickly changed her clothes and left to report this to the Pavilion Owner, one of the most powerful people on the human continent.
"You can let go of my hand now. Any more, and you will be asking for your own death," Ingrid said as they left the pavilion.
"Nope. How else am I going to tell everyone you are now mine?" Kent said, looking at her.
"Who said I am yours?" Ingrid asked with a raised eyebrow.
"So you’re telling me you wouldn’t want to experience what you saw at that auction house?" Kent asked.
"That..." Ingrid’s voice faltered. Indeed, she wanted that dick inside her. She just didn’t know how to go about it yet.
Of course, she was also holding back because of her master. Her master was practically her mother, and she wanted her permission first.
Though she craved him, her obedience to her master was something she didn’t take for granted. Her master was a monster...
She made Ingrid into everything she was and is now, so no matter what, she wouldn’t disobey her master—even if it was for her carnal desires.

"Don’t worry, I’m not going to leave you hanging like that. Though I didn’t know who you were back then, I always had you in my mind and planned to look for you. Now that I have you in my arms, you’ll soon be screaming in my bed," Kent laughed, making Ingrid blush deeply.
Unfortunately, they were out of the pavilion, so all the disgraced disciples waiting outside saw this sight, and it burned their hearts to the core.
"Brat, let go of Big Sister Ingrid’s hand!" A spear arrived in front of Kent, threatening to impale him to the ground. However, no one other than Randy caught it.
Kent, however, didn’t even flinch.
"You are Kent," Randy said. "I am Randy, and I challenge you to a duel. If you have the balls, accept, and let’s see if you can remain standing," he challenged, and the whole place turned quiet.
It was very sudden and perhaps impulsive, but they all wanted to hear Kent’s answer. They were very angry at the moment...
Kent looked at Randy from head to toe and smirked.
"Why don’t we put some stakes on it?" Kent said, showing he had accepted the challenge.
"If you win, I will give you my spot in the upcoming sect competition," Randy declared, making everyone gape in shock.
There were over 100 core disciples in the sect, and only 27 were selected to represent the Divine Palace Sect, with Randy being one of the 27. So, offering his spot... was just too much.

"Sorry, fellas, I am richer than your families combined, so next time, cut your coat according to your size," Kent said.
He wasn’t ready to let this slide.
He knew from high school that if you let your bullies keep bullying you for long, they would see themselves as supreme.
So he made it clear now—he wasn’t about to let the rich and privileged have their way with him.
They had money, but he was richer.
He could only watch them despair since they couldn’t beat him in that field.
As expected, the manager came and gently led the disciples out.
She wasn’t about to pass up on 500 million.
If there are rich brats, then there is a rich, arrogant chaos dragon currently willing to give her 500 million.
She will become the employee of the decade at this point.
After Randy and his minions were led away, Ingrid sighed.
"You do know that after leaving this place, everyone will want to kill you, right?" she said, but Kent just brushed it off.
"They shouldn’t opt for a deathmatch, though.
Defeating them will suffice, considering I don’t want to anger some truly dangerous people, like the Tower Masters, by going on a killing spree," Kent said, taking his last bite.
"Are you looking down on core disciples?" Ingrid asked.
"No... but I don’t think they should look down on me, though.
You know what they say, appearances can be deceiving sometimes."
Of course, Kent was looking down on them.
It was his arrogance getting the best of him.
But if you were to ask whether he had the qualifications to look down on them... the answer is yes.
Most of the core disciples have just entered the next stage of their cultivation.
Most were at the peak of the Root Sage cultivation realm, with a few already at the Root Great Sage realm.
However, none could boast of possessing prowess like Kent.
In the path of swordsmanship, he possessed all three Aspects: Sword Qi, Sword Intent, and Sword Body.
That alone was enough for him to compare himself to a Sword Saint.
"You should be careful...
I can’t save you from everyone," Ingrid said, bringing a smile to Kent’s face.
"The fact that you even consider saving me makes all the difference here," Kent said, teasing her.
As expected, Ingrid blushed slightly, but she turned away from him.
"I only hope you can be this arrogant later on." Ingrid stood up and was ready to leave, but Kent held her hand and dragged her closer to him before holding onto her waist.
He moved her closer to himself and gently brushed his thumb across her lips before licking it...
The action was so seductive that Ingrid’s body shuddered in his grip.𝒇𝒓𝙚𝒆𝔀𝓮𝓫𝒏𝓸𝙫𝓮𝓵.𝓬𝙤𝙢
"You should pay attention to how you eat...
You wouldn’t want to leave food remains on your lips," Kent said, still holding her close to his body.
Ingrid, who had been in a state of shock throughout the dinner, wasn’t aware of the food that remained stuck to her lips.
Kent smiled at her expression and then let go of her waist, making sure his hands brushed across her butt, giving it a gentle massage.
Ingrid’s body shuddered again, but Kent just smiled and dragged her away, holding her hand.
Now that he was done eating, he could only continue with the tour.
"Here you go, as promised," Kent said, handing over the 500 million spirit stones to the manager under the shocked expressions of all the workers present.
"I really enjoyed the food here.
I will come back soon, perhaps with a few friends.
I hope we will be treated well." The manager and the workers nodded.
Kent nodded back at them and walked away, holding Ingrid’s hand.
The workers could only stare at him with gazes filled with reverence.
500 million... each worker would be earning a couple of millions then.
They were super excited.
The manager quickly changed her clothes and left to report this to the Pavilion Owner, one of the most powerful people on the human continent.
"You can let go of my hand now.
Any more, and you will be asking for your own death," Ingrid said as they left the pavilion.
"Nope.
How else am I going to tell everyone you are now mine?" Kent said, looking at her.
"Who said I am yours?" Ingrid asked with a raised eyebrow.
"So you’re telling me you wouldn’t want to experience what you saw at that auction house?" Kent asked.
"That..." Ingrid’s voice faltered.
Indeed, she wanted that dick inside her.
She just didn’t know how to go about it yet.
Of course, she was also holding back because of her master.
Her master was practically her mother, and she wanted her permission first.
Though she craved him, her obedience to her master was something she didn’t take for granted.
Her master was a monster...
She made Ingrid into everything she was and is now, so no matter what, she wouldn’t disobey her master—even if it was for her carnal desires.
"Don’t worry, I’m not going to leave you hanging like that.
Though I didn’t know who you were back then, I always had you in my mind and planned to look for you.
Now that I have you in my arms, you’ll soon be screaming in my bed," Kent laughed, making Ingrid blush deeply.
Unfortunately, they were out of the pavilion, so all the disgraced disciples waiting outside saw this sight, and it burned their hearts to the core.
"Brat, let go of Big Sister Ingrid’s hand!" A spear arrived in front of Kent, threatening to impale him to the ground.
However, no one other than Randy caught it.
Kent, however, didn’t even flinch.
"You are Kent," Randy said.
"I am Randy, and I challenge you to a duel.
If you have the balls, accept, and let’s see if you can remain standing," he challenged, and the whole place turned quiet.
It was very sudden and perhaps impulsive, but they all wanted to hear Kent’s answer.
They were very angry at the moment...
Kent looked at Randy from head to toe and smirked.
"Why don’t we put some stakes on it?" Kent said, showing he had accepted the challenge.
"If you win, I will give you my spot in the upcoming sect competition," Randy declared, making everyone gape in shock.
There were over 100 core disciples in the sect, and only 27 were selected to represent the Divine Palace Sect, with Randy being one of the 27.
So, offering his spot... was just too much.

chapters.title: Chapter 198: Cocky
paragraphs: The Sect Competition is organized once every two years, with over 20 sects participating. Twenty-seven core disciples from each sect are selected to represent their sect, so every core disciple strives to be among the chosen every two years.
Of course, it’s just a competition, so why go through all this trouble just to raise your merit and become part of the selected?𝙛𝒓𝓮𝙚𝔀𝒆𝒃𝓷𝒐𝓿𝙚𝓵.𝙘𝒐𝒎

The answer lies mainly in the follow-up competition after the sect competition—the Kingdom Genius Competition. This competition and the Saint/Saintess Competition are nearly on the same level of prestige.
Twenty-seven disciples will represent their sects; from these 27, the top seven will go on to represent their kingdoms in the Kingdom Genius Competition.
Those who seek fame and power mostly wouldn’t let this chance pass. The Genius Competition will elevate them to a level only a few could measure up to.
The rewards are also very generous, so while the sect competition is like an audition, it’s the most important stage where the best of the best will be selected.
Nobody would be stupid enough to give it away.
The Divine Palace Sect has already selected 25 disciples from the Sword, Spear, Archer, Body, Soul, Mage, and Alchemy factions...with two slots left for disciples who can prove they are worthy.
Randy was part of the selected few, so to put that on the line...one could tell he really meant the challenge, and Kent was doomed.

"You can keep your slot...I don’t want it. However, that doesn’t mean I won’t beat you up. After all, my Ingrid told me two slots are available for any disciple to challenge and claim. Beating you up will win me that slot.
Plus, why would I want everyone to hate me for taking the slot of their one true genius?" Kent said with a smile.
Everyone was looking at him with different expressions. They just didn’t understand how he could be this chill.
And what the fuck does he mean he doesn’t want everyone to hate him...everyone already hates him.

"Of course, since there has to be a stake in this, why don’t I suggest you call me Big Brother Kent for an entire year after I beat you up? Of course, you don’t have to worry about reneging on that deal...if I can beat you up so you call me Big Brother, I can beat you up later too."
The fuming disciples were all glaring at Kent with murderous eyes.

"Of course, if you manage to defeat me, which I doubt will happen, I will grant any request you make, even if it’s for me to slit my own throat. That is good enough, right?" Kent said, and this time, a few people reacted, displaying shocked expressions.
"How can this be enforced?" a disciple asked.
"You don’t have to worry about that. There is someone here who can enforce it," Kent said, turning to his left. "Isn’t that right, Tower Master?"
Everyone turned to the direction he was looking at. At first, they saw no one, but a few seconds later, a beautiful lady appeared. Another second later, the Sword Gate Master appeared.
Both the Sword and Spear Gates have women as gate masters. The rest are dudes with beards.
"Since the Gate Masters are here, do you think I will lie? If your genius manages to beat me, I will grant him whatever request he has.
Now, if you losers have nothing to say, I will be on my way." Kent held Ingrid’s hand and turned to Randy. "You can pick a place and time. I will be going now."
With that, Kent, still holding Ingrid’s hand, left the place. They all could only watch in stunned silence as the brat walked away.
The two gate masters looked at each other and vanished into thin air. The next time they appeared, they were in a lush garden.
"Your disciple is cocky...but handsome," the Spear Gate Master said. She is Spear Sage Camilla, one of the most dangerous women on the human continent and perhaps the entire world.
She is very strong, with only a couple of shortcomings below the Sword Gate Master.
"Oh, he is cocky alright...but I don’t know about handsome," Gate Master Mara said.
"Please don’t lie to yourself. That brat is handsome alright...I wouldn’t mind making him my boy toy," Gate Master Camilla said with a smirk.
"Tsk...what does a hundred-year-old virgin know about boy toys?" Gate Master Mara sneered.

"As if you are any different," the two ladies teased, smiling at each other. They are friends to a certain extent, so while there are rivalries between the gates, the two being the only ladies had to band together.
"But you must be worried for your disciple, right? I mean, you saw that brat—he wasn’t even placing him in his eyes," Gate Master Mara asked.

"I saw that, and yes, I am worried. For some reason, even I became scared of him when he discovered us. I mean, not even a peak Root Great Sage could have sensed us. Something about him scares me," Gate Master Camilla said.
Gate Master Mara nodded. "Same here. I don’t know how, but he scares me."
"Then why do you want to kill him...and please don’t say it was because of what he did to your disciples," Gate Master Camilla asked.
"Who said I want to kill him? I just wanted to discipline him...unfortunately, I never got the chance since his master wouldn’t let me see him."
"Then should we kidnap him and take him to a secret place so you can beat him up? I mean, he is in my domain now...I can make up an excuse," Gate Master Camilla offered.
"Why, are you a child? Kidnapping him would be mercy...I will set him up in the coming days and then have my way with him from there," Gate Master Mara said with a smile.

"Just don’t kill him. Though he is still weak, he might just become a good toy to finally become a woman. I wouldn’t mind at all," Gate Master Camilla said, licking her lips, making Gate Master Mara stare at her in disdain.
"Don’t look at me with those beautiful blue eyes. I have lived for over a hundred years already, and having fun here and there is not bad at all. You should try it sometime."
Gate Master Mara just ignored her. She was currently tracking Kent, who was making his way toward the Spear Saintess’s home.

"But you should warn your disciple, though. This brat will just make him lose face," Gate Master Mara said, knowing Kent wasn’t about to lose, considering she felt his aura firsthand—and that was when he was just a Master Swordsman.

"I won’t. That disciple, Randy, seems to still have the mindset of the rich and entitled. These children from noble homes never learn to respect, so if your disciple is capable, let him teach him a lesson.
Of course, this will also give me the opportunity and excuse to invite him over." Gate Master Camilla laughed at the expression on Gate Master Mara’s face.
Though she wasn’t as unruly as Gate Master Camilla, her interest in Kent started getting the best of her.
The coming days will be rough for her...
